title: Move stream creation onto decodeQueue + fix decoder control/loop races
description:
PROBLEM: stream start is synchronous blocking I/O on whatever thread handles the STRM command. startDecodingFromURL (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:891-1049) calls BASS_StreamCreateURL (synchronous HTTP connect, up to BASS NET_TIMEOUT ~5s) and initializePushStream calls AVAudioSession.setPreferredSampleRate — today this stalls the SlimProto socket queue (delaying all server commands); after the boundary marshal it would freeze the UI instead.

Also fix the decoder control-plane vs decode-loop races (same subsystem, same landing):
- decoderStream lifecycle: during a manual skip, stopDecoding() (frees stream, isDecoding=false) then startDecodingFromURL() (creates NEW stream, assigns decoderStream, isDecoding=true later at :1044). The OLD decode loop on decodeQueue can wake in the window where decoderStream = new handle but isDecoding still false → breaks → its cleanup (:1400-1403) frees the NEW decoder stream and zeroes it → queued new loop exits instantly → silently dead track.
- flushBuffer() resets totalBytesPushed=0 (:1119/:1138) on the caller thread while the decode loop may concurrently do totalBytesPushed += bytesRead (:1379) → corrupted boundary/STMl math.
- skipAheadBytesRemaining (:289, :579): comment claims "thread-safe because decoder loop runs on decodeQueue exclusively" — false; skipAhead() is called from another thread.

FIX SHAPE: make decodeQueue the sole owner of decoder mutable state. Control methods (startDecodingFromURL, stopDecoding, flushBuffer, skipAhead) enqueue onto decodeQueue (async from main); BASS_StreamCreateURL then naturally runs off-main on decodeQueue. Add a generation/epoch counter so a superseded decode loop exits without touching current-generation handles (pattern already exists for pauseGeneration :301). Keep delegate callbacks marshaled to main as today.

TEST: rapid manual skips (5x fast) over slow network — no dead tracks, no UI freeze; gapless boundary math still exact (BOUNDARY logs show delta ~0); Phase 1 device gate.
acceptance_criteria: BASS_StreamCreateURL never runs on main or the socket queue; decoder state owned by decodeQueue; rapid-skip stress produces no dead tracks; boundary accuracy unchanged
close_reason: decodeQueue owns stream+loop (inline loop, serial ordering), decodeGeneration supersede, stateLock critical sections for write-position math, delegate/@Published marshals, throttled-chunk counter fix. Adversarial 8-angle review run; 6 findings fixed. Unit tests green both platforms. Rapid-skip + gapless boundary accuracy need the phase device gate. (--force: 433.1 intentionally open pending device tests.)

title: Marshal SlimProto delegate boundary to main thread (kill the race cluster)
description:
PROBLEM (audit's #1 systemic finding): all server commands are processed on the GCDAsyncSocket delegate queue (SlimProtoClient.swift:90 → coordinator.slimProtoDidReceiveCommand :849-860 → commandHandler.processCommand, no hop). BASS/decoder delegate callbacks marshal to MAIN, timers live on main, UI on main. Result: plain non-atomic state is read/written across threads with no synchronization. Concrete races (all verified):
- expectingGaplessTransition: written on main in sendTrackDecodeComplete (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1332), read/cleared on socket queue in didStartDirectStream (:1160, :1171). Stale read → next track treated non-gapless → mid-playback flush → audible gap. The comment at :1329 shows this race was fought before; ordering the write "before STMd" does not establish cross-thread happens-before.
- waitingForNextTrack: set on main (SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:634), read on socket queue (:566) → false "playlist ended" (STMu + stop).
- pendingUnpauseSTMs (:1151/:1195 socket queue vs handleDecoderDidStartPlayback ~:2601 main) → lost/duplicate STMs breaks the autostart-0 unpause handshake.
- isPausedByLockScreen, wasPlayingBeforeDisconnect, pendingRecoveryTrigger, isAppInBackground, SimpleTimeTracker fields, SlimProtoClient.isConnected — same pattern.
- Timers (playbackHeartbeatTimer :398-405, metadata timers) installed on main, invalidate()d from socket queue — Apple requires invalidation from the installing thread; symptom: duplicate heartbeats / zombie STMt after STMp.
- NotificationCenter.post(.slimProtoDidConnect) (:808) fires CarPlay observers on the socket queue.

FIX: single-threaded control plane on main, squeezelite-style. Either (a) hop at the delegate boundary: slimProtoDidReceiveCommand/DidConnect/DidDisconnect wrap their bodies in DispatchQueue.main.async, or (b) construct GCDAsyncSocket with delegateQueue: .main. Option (b) is smaller but changes read-callback timing; (a) is explicit and keeps socket I/O off main. Remove the now-redundant ad hoc hops (e.g. SETD at SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:104, notifyTrackEnded marshal at SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:155).

CRITICAL COMPANION (same landing, see stream-creation issue): once command handling is on main, BASS_StreamCreateURL (blocking network, up to 5s NET_TIMEOUT) inside startDecodingFromURL would freeze the UI — the stream-creation offload MUST land in the same build.

TEST: full Phase 1 device gate (see phase bead). Also thread-sanitizer run of the unit suite if practical.
acceptance_criteria: All coordinator/commandHandler state mutations happen on main; no Timer is invalidated cross-thread; gapless + unpause handshake + lock-screen state survive full regression on both platforms
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 1: Threading model — single-threaded control plane
description:
The structural fix: give the control plane a single-threaded model (main thread), matching squeezelite's single-threaded slimproto loop. This eliminates the audit's largest finding — pervasive unsynchronized state shared between the GCDAsyncSocket delegate queue, main thread, and decode queue.

Highest-risk phase — do it in isolation, nothing else in the same builds.

DEVICE TEST GATE (full regression, iOS + tvOS):
- Gapless album playback across 3+ boundaries (listen for seams; server-oracle: playlist_cur_index advances exactly at boundaries, time advances ~1x).
- Rapid manual skips (hammer next 5x), skip during last 30s of a track (post-STMd window), seek, pause/resume.
- Lock screen + CarPlay controls; volume from server UI (audg).
- Background >45s then foreground (silent recovery, no audio burst); background <45s quick resume.
- Kill/restart LMS mid-playback → reconnect + playlist-jump recovery.
- UI responsiveness during track start on a slow/cellular connection (BASS_StreamCreateURL must not block main).
close_reason: Re-close: state lost to jsonl auto-reimport. Originally fixed+committed on playback-audit branches; phase 0/1 device gates passed by user 2026-07-10.

title: STAT jiffies overflow crashes app when device uptime > 49.7 days
description: 21 of 26 App Store crash logs (1.7.6–1.7.8) are 'Double value cannot be converted to UInt32' in SlimProtoClient.sendStatus. Cause: 'UInt32(ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime * 1000)' at SlimProtoClient.swift:404 traps once uptime exceeds UInt32.max ms (~49.7 days). iPhones routinely stay up for months, and every STAT send crashes, so the app is 100% unusable for affected users until they reboot the phone. Same bug in SlimProtoCoordinator.gettime_ms() at line 1474. Fix: wrap modulo 2^32 like squeezelite's gettime_ms (u32 wraparound is expected by the server), e.g. UInt32((UInt64(uptime*1000)) & 0xFFFFFFFF) or UInt32(truncatingIfNeeded: Int64(...)). Both sites must use the same wrapping so jiffies math stays consistent.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix authentication missing from metadata, cover art, and playback control requests
description:
## Problem
GitHub Issue #62 - Users with password-protected LMS servers can connect and play audio, but cover art and metadata don't load on lock screen, Control Center, or CarPlay. Two users confirmed removing the password fixes it.

## Root Cause
The auth implementation (Dec 2025) correctly injects credentials into audio stream URLs and some JSON-RPC calls, but missed several HTTP request paths:

1. **sendJSONCommand()** (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:~1568) - Play/pause/skip commands from lock screen/CarPlay fail silently on auth servers. No auth header.
2. **fetchCurrentTrackMetadata()** (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:~1875) - Track title/artist/album/artwork URL never fetched. No auth header.
3. **parseTrackMetadata() artwork URL** (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:~1928-1932) - Artwork URLs constructed without credentials, so image fetch returns 401.
4. **NowPlayingManager.loadArtwork()** (NowPlayingManager.swift:~345) - Lock screen/Control Center artwork fetch uses raw URL with no auth.
5. **CarPlaySceneDelegate.loadArtwork()** (CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:~787) - CarPlay artwork fetch has no auth header.

## Fix
Add generateAuthHeader() / injectCredentialsIntoURL() calls to all 5 locations, matching the existing pattern used in fetchServerTime() and sendJSONRPCCommandDirect().

## Files to Modify
- SlimProtoCoordinator.swift (3 fixes: sendJSONCommand, fetchCurrentTrackMetadata, parseTrackMetadata)
- NowPlayingManager.swift (1 fix: loadArtwork)
- CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift (1 fix: loadArtwork)

## External Reference
GitHub Issue #62: Could not control playback in lock screen
close_reason: Fixed in commit a756ae3 on fix/auth-metadata-cover-art branch. Added auth headers to all 5 missed HTTP request paths.

title: Fix intermittent pause command failures during phone calls and CarPlay disconnect
description:
## Problem Summary
Pause commands sent to LMS server are intermittently failing in two scenarios:

### Issue A: Phone call interruption - playback resumes DURING call
**Observed behavior:** Call comes in → app pauses server (works) → ~5 seconds later playback resumes while still on phone call
**Expected behavior:** Playback should stay paused until call ends

**Root cause analysis:**
- `PlaybackSessionController.handleRouteChange()` (line 385-396) has auto-resume logic
- Checks `!currentHasPhoneRoute && interruptionContext != nil` and sends play command
- iOS may send route change notifications mid-call that trick app into thinking call ended
- Race condition between `handleInterruption` and `handleRouteChange` handlers

### Issue B: CarPlay disconnect - pause never reaches server  
**Observed behavior:** Exit car on track 1, return to find album on track 10 (server played entire time)
**Expected behavior:** Server should pause when disconnecting from CarPlay

**Root cause analysis:**
- `handleCarPlayDisconnected()` sends pause via fire-and-forget pattern
- No confirmation that server received/executed pause command
- Network transitioning (car WiFi → cellular) when exiting car likely causes command to fail silently
- Current retry logic (2 retries with 2s delay) may not handle network transition window

## Files involved
- PlaybackSessionController.swift:385-396 (route change auto-resume logic)
- PlaybackSessionController.swift:439-455 (CarPlay disconnect handler)
- SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1504-1550 (sendJSONCommand - no confirmation)

## Proposed fix approach

### For Issue A:
1. Add debounce/guard for auto-resume during active interruption
2. Don't trust route changes alone - require both route change AND interruption ended
3. Add minimum interruption duration check (e.g., must be interrupted for 3+ seconds before allowing route-based resume)

### For Issue B:
1. Add confirmation query after pause command (status check to verify `mode: "pause"`)
2. Implement retry with exponential backoff if confirmation fails
3. Consider SlimProto-level pause command as backup (more reliable than HTTP during network transition)
4. Extend background task timeout during network transitions

## Test scenarios
- [ ] Phone call while playing - verify stays paused entire call
- [ ] Short phone call (<10s) - verify resumes correctly after
- [ ] Exit CarPlay while on WiFi - verify pause works
- [ ] Exit CarPlay triggering WiFi→cellular transition - verify pause works
- [ ] Check server status after CarPlay disconnect to confirm paused state

title: CarPlay connection failure - no retry mechanism when server unreachable
description:
## Problem

When entering car and launching LyrPlay via CarPlay:
1. Press LyrPlay button in CarPlay
2. See "Loading" async spinner for cover art/albums/playlists
3. Loading never completes - spinner stays forever
4. Press resume playback - nothing happens
5. Open app on iOS device - "Cannot connect to server" popup appears

**Root Cause**: CarPlay UI tried to connect but server was unreachable. No retry mechanism or error handling when initial connection fails.

## Expected Behavior

When CarPlay connection fails:
1. Show error state in CarPlay UI (not infinite loading)
2. Provide "Retry Connection" button/option
3. Or auto-retry with exponential backoff
4. Display helpful error message ("Server unreachable - check network")

## Current Behavior

- Infinite loading spinner in CarPlay
- No error feedback to user
- No way to retry from CarPlay
- Must open phone app to see actual error

## Impact

- User gets stuck in car with non-functional CarPlay UI
- Must physically interact with phone (unsafe while driving)
- Poor UX - looks like app is broken, not network issue

## Proposed Solution

### Option 1: Retry Button
- Detect connection failure in CarPlaySceneDelegate
- Show error template with "Retry" button
- Allow user to manually retry connection

### Option 2: Auto-Retry with Timeout
- Auto-retry 3 times with 2s, 4s, 8s delays
- Show error after all retries fail
- Provide "Retry Now" button

### Option 3: Background Connection Monitor
- Start background connection attempt when CarPlay connects
- Show placeholder UI while connecting
- Auto-refresh UI when connection succeeds
- Show error state if connection times out

## Files Likely Involved

- **CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift**: CarPlay lifecycle and template management
- **SlimProtoCoordinator.swift**: Connection management and error handling
- **SettingsManager.swift**: Server configuration and connection state

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] Connect CarPlay with LMS server offline
- [ ] Verify error state shows (not infinite spinner)
- [ ] Test retry mechanism works
- [ ] Verify auto-recovery when server comes online
- [ ] Test with VPN disconnected (common car scenario)
- [ ] Verify main app shows same connection state

## Related Issues

This affects CarPlay Browse interface (Phase 2) - connection reliability is critical for safety.
notes:
## Implementation Complete - PENDING TESTING

Fixed CarPlay connection failure infinite loading spinner issue with comprehensive error handling and retry mechanism.

### Changes Made (CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift)

**1. Connection State Check (Line 53-65)**
- Added 1-second delay after coordinator.connect() to allow async connection
- Checks coordinator.isConnected before attempting data fetch
- Shows error state immediately if connection fails

**2. Timeout Protection (Line 895-913)**
- Replaced group.notify() with group.wait(timeout: 5.0)
- Prevents infinite loading if network requests hang
- Shows error state on timeout

**3. Connection Error UI (Line 827-881)**
- New showConnectionError() method
- Displays clear error message: "Cannot Connect to Server"
- Provides "Retry Connection" button
- Keeps "Resume Playback" available even when disconnected

**4. Retry Mechanism (Line 883-934)**
- New retryConnection() method
- Shows "Connecting..." loading state during retry
- Reinitializes coordinator if needed, or reconnects existing one
- 2-second timeout to check connection status
- On success: loads home template data
- On failure: shows error state again

### User Experience Improvements
✅ No more infinite loading spinner
✅ Clear error feedback when server unreachable
✅ One-tap retry from CarPlay (no phone interaction needed)
✅ Safe for use while driving (tap retry, don't fumble with phone)
✅ Resume playback still available even when disconnected

### Testing Required (Tomorrow)
- [ ] Test with airplane mode enabled
- [ ] Test with VPN disconnected (Tailscale scenario)
- [ ] Test with LMS server offline
- [ ] Test network timeout (5s timeout triggers error)
- [ ] Test successful retry after connection restored
- [ ] Test Resume Playback button works in error state

### Code Status
✅ Implementation complete
✅ Compiles successfully
⏳ Awaiting real-world CarPlay testing

title: Investigate USB DAC reinit not working - testers report issues
description:
## Issue Report

Testers report that BASS_DEVICE_REINIT implementation (build 7) is not working correctly with USB DACs.

## What We Implemented (Build 7)

Code in AudioStreamDecoder.swift:636-686:
1. Check device rate with BASS_GetInfo()
2. If mismatch with stream rate, call BASS_Init with BASS_DEVICE_REINIT
3. Verify final device rate

## Potential Issues to Check

### 1. Initial BASS_Init Might Block Reinit

**AudioPlayer.swift:145** initializes BASS once at 48kHz:
\`\`\`swift
let targetRate: DWORD = 48000
let result = BASS_Init(-1, targetRate, DWORD(BASS_DEVICE_FREQ), nil, nil)
\`\`\`

**Question**: Does initial BASS_Init with BASS_DEVICE_FREQ lock the device at 48kHz?

### 2. Missing BASS_DEVICE_FREQ on Reinit?

**AudioStreamDecoder.swift:651** does reinit with:
\`\`\`swift
BASS_Init(-1, DWORD(actualSampleRate), DWORD(BASS_DEVICE_FREQ | BASS_DEVICE_REINIT), nil, nil)
\`\`\`

This looks correct - has both flags.

### 3. iOS Session Rate Conflict?

**PlaybackSessionController.swift:156** sets:
\`\`\`swift
try session.setPreferredSampleRate(48000)
\`\`\`

**Question**: Does iOS AVAudioSession lock prevent BASS from changing hardware rate?

### 4. Timing Issue?

Maybe BASS_DEVICE_REINIT needs to happen BEFORE creating the stream decoder, not during startDecodingFromURL()?

## Debug Steps Needed

1. **Add logging before/after BASS_Init** to see if initial init locks device
2. **Check BASS_ErrorGetCode** when BASS_DEVICE_REINIT fails
3. **Test without AVAudioSession.setPreferredSampleRate** to see if iOS is blocking
4. **Move reinit earlier** - try before decoder creation instead of during stream start

## Questions for un4seen Forum

1. Does initial BASS_Init with BASS_DEVICE_FREQ lock the device rate?
2. Can BASS_DEVICE_REINIT change from 48kHz→96kHz→192kHz dynamically?
3. Does iOS AVAudioSession.preferredSampleRate interfere with BASS rate changes?
4. Should we NOT use BASS_DEVICE_FREQ on initial init, only on BASS_DEVICE_REINIT?

## Test Logs Needed from Testers

- What does app log show for device reinit?
- What sample rate does DAC display show?
- What does iOS Audio MIDI Setup show for the device?
- Does it work for ANY high-res file or completely fails?
notes:
## Ian's Response (Forum Topic 20831)

**Forum Link:** https://www.un4seen.com/forum/?topic=20831.0

Ian confirmed the correct approach for iOS bit-perfect playback:

### Recommended Method: AVAudioSession.setPreferredSampleRate

**Quote from Ian:**
> "You can use AVAudioSession to set the sample rate, eg:
> [[AVAudioSession sharedInstance] setPreferredSampleRate:chaninfo.freq error:nil];
> 
> BASS will also detect when the output rate is changed."

### Implementation Updated (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:636-676)

**What Changed:**
- ❌ Removed BASS_DEVICE_REINIT approach (was correct but not iOS-preferred)
- ✅ Now using AVAudioSession.setPreferredSampleRate per Ian's guidance
- ✅ BASS automatically detects the rate change - no manual reinit needed

**New Code Flow:**
1. Check current iOS session sample rate
2. If mismatch with content, call setPreferredSampleRate
3. BASS detects the change automatically
4. Verify final rates with BASS_GetInfo + AVAudioSession

**Benefits:**
- Simpler than BASS_DEVICE_REINIT
- iOS-native approach
- BASS handles detection automatically
- Works with external DACs that support rate switching

### Testing Needed

Rebuild and test with USB DAC:
- 96kHz FLAC → DAC should show 96kHz
- 192kHz FLAC → DAC should show 192kHz  
- 44.1kHz MP3 → DAC should show 44.1kHz
- Built-in speaker → Should gracefully report 48kHz limitation

Check console logs for:
- ✅ "Bit-perfect playback: XXHz → XXHz"
- ℹ️ "Device limited to 48kHz" (for built-in audio)

title: Phase 1A: Research all BASS streaming modes for auth compatibility
description:
Investigate and document all BASS streaming modes to ensure authentication headers work everywhere.

CRITICAL RESEARCH NEEDED:
User reports two streaming modes exist:
1. Old URL streaming (legacy FLAC workaround)
2. Push streaming (gapless playback)

Tasks:
1. Search codebase for ALL BASS_StreamCreateURL calls
2. Search for BASS_StreamCreate (push stream with STREAMPROC)
3. Identify where FLAC auto-routing decision is made
4. Document all audio stream creation paths
5. Verify auth header mechanism works for BOTH modes

Files to Investigate:
- AudioPlayer.swift (all stream creation functions)
- SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift (STRM command handling)
- CLAUDE.md (references to "FLAC Auto-Routing" and "legacy URL streaming")

Expected Findings:
- List all stream creation entry points
- Document differences between modes
- Identify if BASS_CONFIG_NET_AGENT works for both
- Alternative: custom DOWNLOADPROC if needed for one mode

Deliverable:
- Technical document listing all streaming paths
- Recommendation for where to inject auth headers
notes:
CRITICAL DISCOVERY - BASS does NOT support custom HTTP headers!

INITIAL ASSUMPTION (WRONG):
❌ Use BASS_SetConfigPtr(BASS_CONFIG_NET_AGENT) to inject Authorization headers
❌ BASS_CONFIG_NET_AGENT would apply to all BASS_StreamCreateURL calls

ACTUAL FINDINGS:
✅ BASS_CONFIG_NET_AGENT is for User-Agent header ONLY
✅ BASS has NO built-in support for custom HTTP headers
✅ Attempting to use it for Authorization caused crashes (EXC_BAD_ACCESS)

CORRECT APPROACH (from LMS documentation):
✅ LMS supports URL-embedded credentials: http://username:password@server:port/stream.mp3
✅ Documented in slimserver/HTML/EN/html/docs/remotestreaming.html:
   "If you are using the server's password security, you'll need to use a 
    slightly modified URL like this: http://username:password@localhost:9000/stream.mp3"
✅ BASS supports standard HTTP URL credentials automatically

STREAMING ARCHITECTURE (confirmed):
Both streaming modes use BASS_StreamCreateURL():
1. AudioStreamDecoder:610 - decode-only for gapless playback
2. AudioPlayer:942 - direct playback mode

URL credential injection works for BOTH because it's done BEFORE the URL reaches BASS.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- SettingsManager.injectCredentialsIntoURL() modifies stream URLs
- SlimProtoCommandHandler calls this before passing URL to AudioPlayer
- URLComponents safely handles special characters in username/password
- No BASS configuration changes needed

LMS SERVER VALIDATION:
- slimserver/Slim/Web/HTTP.pm validates HTTP Basic Auth for ALL requests
- checkAuthorization() function (line 2550) validates credentials
- Works for both WebView access AND stream URLs
- Server returns 401 WWW-Authenticate if auth fails

UPDATED CLAUDE.md:
- Removed "FLAC Auto-Routing" references (no longer exists)
- Updated to "Unified Gapless Architecture" 
- All formats use push stream architecture

title: tvOS radio artwork blips every 15s - radio metadata poll re-downloads unchanged cover
description: Forum report (castalla #726, 2026-07-12): artwork flashes/blips every ~10-15s on ALL streaming radio stations on tvOS; Tidal/iBroadcast fine. Root cause: the 15s radio metadata refresh timer (duration=0 streams only, which is why track content is unaffected) calls updateTrackMetadata unconditionally each tick -> loadArtwork re-downloads the cover -> applyArtwork publishes a NEW UIImage instance even when pixels are identical -> tvOS NowPlayingView animates on currentArtwork change (UIImage equality = reference identity) -> visible crossfade blip. Also wasteful: re-downloads up to 2048px art every 15s. Fix: dedupe in NowPlayingManager - skip the artwork reload when the incoming artwork URL matches the currently painted one (latched only on successful load so failures retry). Bonus: kills the crossfade between same-album consecutive tracks.
close_reason: Field-verified 2026-07-15 (castalla, tvOS build 20): radio artwork no longer blips - painted-URL latch dedupes the 15s poll's re-download

title: Decoder stream creation failure is terminal - no STMn, playback dies silently (tester VPN stops)
description: Tester report: streaming over WireGuard VPN in car - player just stopped mid-playlist, needed manual skip or hard restart to revive; iPeng fine in same conditions. Owner also saw a missed track transition. Captured in the 2026-07-12 device log: TRACK DECODE COMPLETE (STMd) at 12:32:10, VPN blip, then 'Decoder stream creation failed: 40' (BASS_ERROR_TIMEOUT) at 12:32:22 for the next track - and the guard at AudioStreamDecoder startDecodingFromURL was a bare return: no retry, no delegate, no STMn. Current track drains ~30s buffer then dead air. Rarely seen before epic 433 because the (buggy) STMd status-poll heuristic removed in nzj was accidentally rescuing this dead state. Fix: creation-failure guard now calls audioStreamDecoderDidEncounterError -> AudioManager -> STMn, so the server marks the track failed and advances (same recovery the tester did manually). Decode-loop error paths already did this; only the creation guard was mute. Follow-up worth investigating separately: mid-track HTTP death can masquerade as natural decode end (ENDED + disconnected) - possible truncated-track/early-boundary case.
close_reason: Field-verified 2026-07-15 (builds 32/33): dead-spot no longer freezes at playing/0:00 - creation-failure STMn goes out (generation-gated, round-2 fix 33a2faf) and the server advances

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text: Field failure in build 31 (2026-07-14 dead spot, diagnostic log): creation-failure STMn was suppressed because the guard read manualStop, which is only cleared on the success path — a reconnect's strm 'q' right before the recovery stream start left it stale-true. Server froze in playing-at-0.14s zombie state, never recovered even after network restore. Fixed: guard on decode generation (stillCurrent) instead of manualStop. Adversarially reviewed (CONFIRMED-GOOD, all stop/start orderings enumerated; also closes a spurious-STMn hazard for superseded starts). Residual gap noted: STMn sent while slimproto socket is fully down is dropped silently (sendStatus guard) — in this incident the socket was up, so the fix covers it.

title: App-open recovery fires while CarPlay actively playing - pauses live playback ~1s and rewinds to stale position
description: Captured device log 2026-07-12 build 30: opening the phone app during an active CarPlay playback session cold-launches ContentView (phone UI scene was torn down; process alive for CarPlay). The cold-launch recovery gate (ContentView onAppear) checks duration/data/setting but NOT player state - unlike the warm path which skips when Playing. Result: .appOpen trigger -> CarPlay branch -> playlist jump against a LIVE session: strm q pauses playback ~0.9s and jumps to stale saved position (140.02s vs live 148.5s). Fix: handlePendingRecovery .appOpen skips when getPlayerState()==Playing (right altitude - covers cold launch, warm resume, CarPlay branch).
close_reason: Device-verified (build 31+): opening phone app during live CarPlay playback continues seamlessly - appOpen recovery skips when audio is actively playing

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text: Fix committed: handlePendingRecovery .appOpen now skips when getPlayerState()==Playing (nothing to recover; cancelPreMute safety no-op included). Both platforms build, iOS suite passes. Pending device verify: play via CarPlay, open phone app - playback must continue seamlessly, no pause, no position rewind. Log marker: 'App open recovery: already playing - skipping'.

title: End-of-playlist on push path: no STMu at output drain — server stuck in play, Material time sawtooths
close_reason: Fixed: decodeCompletedNaturally latch armed at natural decode completion, consumed by handleBufferEnd on no-pending-track drain → STMu via new sendPlaybackComplete(). Verified server-side semantics against StreamingController Stopped-event table. Device test: play playlist to its true end → clean stop, no sawtooth; also verify normal gapless boundaries unaffected.

title: Lock-screen timer hunts during playlist-jump recovery — server play-point poisoned by stale STAT elapsed
close_reason: Root-caused via server-as-oracle trace: server displayed startOffset + stale client STAT elapsed (dead pre-background stream) for ~0.9s post-jump; app's 3s poll amplified it into visible lock-screen hunting. Fixed in commit 04c1a1c: seed SimpleTimeTracker with the known resume position at jump issue, suppress server-time polls for 3s, skip strm 'q' zero-reset inside the window. Device verification pending (user).

title: Lock-screen playlist-jump recovery: displayed time hunts before settling (post-433.2.2 async start)
description: REGRESSION from 433.2.2 (device gate feedback): trackStartTimeOffset is assigned inside performStartDecoding (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:975), which runs async on decodeQueue. In the window between strm 's' processing and BASS_StreamCreateURL completing, STAT heartbeats/lock-screen fallback compute position from the flushed stream (0) + the OLD track's offset, then snap to the new seek offset when the async start executes — server time follows our STAT so the displayed timer jumps back/forward before settling. FIX: set trackStartTimeOffset synchronously in the startDecodingFromURL wrapper (control plane), matching pre-433.2.2 timing; remove the assignment from performStartDecoding.
close_reason: trackStartTimeOffset set synchronously in startDecodingFromURL wrapper, removed from async performStartDecoding. Unit tests green both platforms. Needs device re-test: lock-screen play after timeout -> time settles immediately without hunting.

title: Paused-session reconnect runs playlist recovery regardless of enableAppOpenRecovery (post-433.1.4)
description: REGRESSION from 433.1.4 (device gate feedback): handlePendingRecovery .networkRestored case (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:766) recovers when wasPlayingBeforeDisconnect || wasPausedBeforeDisconnect and never consults settings.enableAppOpenRecovery. Pre-433.1.4 a paused push stream misreported Stopped, so wasPausedBeforeDisconnect was never set and the paused arm was dead. Now it fires on every paused-session reconnect (e.g. reopen app after long background) — recovery appears 'always on' with the setting off. title: Health-check timer never fires after connect (scheduled on run-loop-less socket queue)
description:
PROBLEM: startHealthMonitoring (SlimProtoConnectionManager.swift:379-387) uses Timer.scheduledTimer, which schedules on the CURRENT thread's run loop. It is invoked from didConnect() (:434+), which runs on the GCDAsyncSocket delegate queue ("com.lmsstream.socket") — a GCD worker thread with NO run loop. The 15s/30s health timer therefore NEVER fires after a fresh connect. scheduleReconnection (:587-593) contains a comment fixing this exact bug class for the reconnect timer; this site was missed. Consequence: half-open TCP (server reboot, AP swap) is never detected via heartbeat timeout; app shows Connected forever. Health monitoring only works today after a background/foreground cycle re-arms it from main.

FIX: replace with the same DispatchQueue.main-based pattern scheduleReconnection uses (DispatchWorkItem/DispatchSourceTimer), or dispatch startHealthMonitoring to main. (Phase 1 will move didConnect to main anyway, but fix this now — it is a one-liner and independently testable.)

TEST: with app idle-connected, hard-kill LMS (or drop server NIC) without closing the socket; app must detect the dead connection and start reconnecting within ~30-45s WITHOUT backgrounding the app.
acceptance_criteria: healthCheckTimer fires on schedule after a fresh connect from the socket queue; half-open connection detected within one heartbeat window
close_reason: Closed

title: AudioPlayer.stop() leaks BASS stream (ChannelStop without StreamFree)
description:
PROBLEM: AudioPlayer.stop() (AudioPlayer.swift:425-438) calls BASS_ChannelStop(currentStream) then sets currentStream = 0 WITHOUT BASS_StreamFree. Compare cleanup() (:760-773) which stops AND frees. Once zeroed, the handle can never be freed — every stop on the legacy URL-stream path leaks the BASS stream and its buffers. BASS_STREAM_AUTOFREE is commented out, so nothing else frees it.

FIX: add BASS_StreamFree(currentStream) in stop() (or route stop() through cleanup()). Keep the cancelPendingResume() ordering used in cleanup().

TEST: play a legacy URL stream (HTTP mode / radio), server stop 'q', repeat several times; verify no handle growth (BASS_ChannelIsActive on old handle returns BASS_ERROR_HANDLE) and playback still restarts cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: stop() frees the stream; repeated stop/start shows no leaked handles; legacy-path playback regression-free
close_reason: Closed

title: iOS hardware volume rocker dies after app suspended (GH#75 regression)
description:
Regression in the GH#75 hardware-volume forwarding feature. Symptom: rocker controls the external player after launch, but stops working once the app is backgrounded long enough to suspend (~1-2 min) — and stays dead until app restart. Works in simulator (never suspends) and for short backgrounds.

ROOT CAUSE (device-verified via logs 2026-06-11): the rocker only engages while the local player is idle, so the app has no background audio and iOS suspends it quickly. After resume, AVAudioSession.outputVolume freezes (stuck at 0.500) and its KVO stops firing, while the MPVolumeView slider keeps tracking the hardware buttons (outVol=0.500 frozen vs sliderVal 0.500->0.562->0.625). Rebuilding the outputVolume observer on foreground does NOT help — a fresh observer is dead too.

FIX (VolumeRockerForwarder.swift): detect presses by polling the MPVolumeView slider value (live in all states) instead of AVAudioSession.outputVolume KVO. Same VolumeRockerLogic (delta->press + recenter), no audio-session management (Critical Rule #2 intact). Also force disengage on willResignActive (applicationState is still .active there, so the old code never disengaged on background) so the engaged state tears down/rebuilds cleanly each cycle.

VERIFIED on device: after a backgrounded+suspended cycle, slider poll detects up/down presses, forwards to Material (Press JS forwarded OK), external player volume changes.
close_reason: Fixed + hardware-verified 2026-06-11: switched press detection from frozen-after-suspend AVAudioSession.outputVolume KVO to MPVolumeView slider polling; added willResignActive disengage. Device log confirms presses detected and forwarded after a suspend cycle.

title: App-open recovery mute is a timing race (intermittent audible playlist jump)
description:
SYMPTOM: After backgrounding >45s and reopening, app-open recovery sometimes plays the playlist jump audibly (seek heard, then mutes) instead of recovering silently. Intermittent — often works, sometimes not.

NOT a recent regression: traced the whole mute/recovery chain. Mute mechanism (muteNextStream, BASS_ATTRIB_VOLDSP 0.001) last changed Oct-Nov 2025 (91315974, 0b464d2, 49f37ce). Trigger classification (pendingRecoveryTrigger/handlePendingRecovery) last changed in c03a5b3 (v1.7.7 #82) and 4624ee4. Last 5-10 commits did not touch it.

ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (timing race): executePlaylistRecovery (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift ~648-665) unmutes on FIXED wall-clock delays: jump response -> +1.5s -> pause -> +2.0s -> disableSilentRecoveryMode() (~3.5s after jump). But muteNextStream only mutes the new stream WHEN it is created (AudioStreamDecoder.startPlayback:736 / AudioPlayer:328), which depends on server/network latency after the noplay=0 jump. If stream-up < 3.5s -> created while muted (silent, OK). If stream-up > 3.5s -> the fixed-delay unmute fires first (muteNextStream=false + restoreDSPGain) -> new stream starts UNMUTED -> audible jump. The 10s recovery-timeout at :584 is a second fixed-delay unmute with the same failure mode. noplay=0 (always play then pause, CLAUDE rule #4) means a real stream always plays; muting it is a race against timers.

PROPOSED FIX: make the unmute EVENT-DRIVEN. Gate disableSilentRecoveryMode() on the stream-established / pause-confirmed event (the audioStreamDecoderDidStartPlayback / STMs callback added in 2387e56) rather than +1.5s/+2.0s guesses. Keep a generous safety timeout as backstop, not the primary path.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: capture [APP-RECOVERY] logs on a failing run. Compare timestamps of 'Playlist jump recovery completed', 'Push stream playback started (muted: YES/NO)', and 'Silent recovery complete - volume restored'. A failing run shows volume restored BEFORE stream started, or 'muted: NO'. Critical path — do not change without a confirming log.

Files: LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift (executePlaylistRecovery ~579-677), LMS_StreamTest/AudioManager.swift (enable/disableSilentRecoveryMode 434-460), LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift (startPlayback ~715-742), LMS_StreamTest/AudioPlayer.swift (~328).
close_reason: Device-verified fixed in iOS build 30: root cause was double-triggered app-open recovery (.networkRestored racing .appOpen) bare-unmuting the first recovery's still-playing muted stream. Fixed via appOpen dedupe, settle-before-unmute early-returns, owner-aware lock rejection, plus t=0 VOL pre-mute and 10-20s mute safety ceiling as defense-in-depth. Diagnosed from on-device diagnostic log captured via the new Copy Diagnostic Log exporter.

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-07-11 code study, owner still hitting ~occasional blips post-build-13).

PRIMARY: mute applied AFTER BASS_ChannelPlay on the push path. AudioStreamDecoder.startPlayback() runs BASS_ChannelPlay(pushStream) at :819 and only then applies BASS_ATTRIB_VOLDSP=0.001 at :826. Same inverted order in the synchronized-start timer path (:481 play, :486 mute). VOLDSP is a DSP gain baked into samples as BASS processes them into the playback buffer — NOT retroactive to already-processed data (unlike BASS_ATTRIB_VOL which applies at output stage). At ChannelPlay, BASS's update thread immediately processes queued push data through the DSP chain at FULL gain to fill the ~500ms playback buffer; the mute set microseconds later only affects data processed after. So up to ~500ms of full-volume audio is committed before the mute lands. Intermittency explained: blip audibility depends on how much decoded data sat in the push queue at play time (fast network/decode = audible; slow = silent). Proof by asymmetry: resumePlayback() (:869 mute before :883 play) and the legacy URL path AudioPlayer.swift (:356 mute before :369 play) have the correct order and don't blip.

SECONDARY: the 3.5s fallback ceiling (SlimProtoCoordinator :768) unmutes unconditionally. If the STMp pause confirmation is slower than 3.5s (slow server/network right after reconnect), gain is restored on a stream still audibly playing — mid-track burst until the pause lands.

PROPOSED FIX (3 small changes):
1. Apply VOLDSP mute at stream CREATION — createPushStream, right after BASS_StreamCreate succeeds (next to the stored-volume application at :768-772): if muteNextStream, set VOLDSP=0.001 before any data can be processed. Airtight for fresh streams regardless of play path.
2. Move the play-time mute applications BEFORE BASS_ChannelPlay in startPlayback() and the sync-start timer (covers pre-existing streams; enableSilentRecoveryMode's applyMuting() already covers the in-flight case).
3. Fallback ceiling: if the push stream is still actively playing when the 3.5s timer fires, call pausePlayback() (local BASS pause — the intended end state is paused anyway) BEFORE restoring gain. Preserves the never-stay-muted guarantee without the audible burst.

Verification plan: unit builds both platforms; on-device: 15-20 app-open cycles after >45s background expecting zero blips; grep logs for 'volume restored (fallback timer)' occurrences — each one is a slow-STMp case that change 3 now protects.

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text: Fix landed (see commit fix(audio): silent-recovery mute...): creation-time + before-play muting via applyMuting() at all 5 play sites, legacy-path replay-gain/mute reorder, settleSilentRecoveryAudio() for both timeout paths. iOS + tvOS suites green. PENDING DEVICE VERIFICATION: 15-20 app-open cycles after >45s background, expect zero blips; also FLAC (legacy URL path) app-open recovery specifically — that path could previously play at full replay gain through the whole recovery window. Log markers: 'muted at stream creation'/'muted before play' = good path; 'fallback timer'/'recovery timeout' with 'pausing locally + retrying server pause' = slow-STMp case now handled.

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text: Root cause of the remaining blip found (user hypothesis confirmed): >45s background with server still holding the player — a stalled push stream auto-resumes at full volume when the suspended socket thaws, inside the 0.5s window before the recovery check runs, and VOLDSP muting cannot silence samples already in the playback buffer. Fix (e2758ac): instant BASS_ATTRIB_VOL=0 pre-mute at t=0 in willEnterForeground + pause stalled channels; outputMuted guards setVolume/getVolume; new streams created in-window come up VOL-muted; audible recoveries fully unmute superseded silent recoveries; 10s→20s mute safety ceiling guarantees never-stuck-silent. Adversarial review caught and fixed: stuck-silent latch on recovery collisions, new-stream VOL bypass, pre-mute landing on in-flight lock-screen resume. Awaiting device verification: 15-20 app-open cycles, watch for PRE-MUTE / MUTE CEILING log markers.

Gen 5 found recovery data consumed by gen 4, took the no-data early-return, and bare-unmuted gen 4's still-playing muted stream at 15.926; only pause landed at 16.815 = ~0.9s blip. title: Push-stream skipAhead is delayed by ~30s buffer drain — multi-room sync can't recover from drift
description:
## Problem

The server-side LMS multi-room sync algorithm (Slim::Player::StreamingController::_CheckSync) sends strm 'a' (skipAhead) commands to lagging players in a sync group every ~1 second. For LyrPlay's push-stream code path (FLAC), the skipAhead correction is buffer-drain-delayed and effectively unbounded:

```
Server (every 2s): skipAhead 13ms
LyrPlay: marks 4608 bytes (12ms) for discard at decoder input
Server (next cycle): still -13ms, skipAhead 13ms  ← no change
... loops forever
```

The decoder-input discard mechanism is correct in concept but takes ~30s to propagate through the BASS push queue (current maxBufferSize = 11_520_000 ≈ 30s at 48kHz stereo float32 + 500ms BASS playback buffer). By the time the discards reach the speaker, the server has issued ~15 corrections totaling 100s of ms, the player overshoots, then pauseForInterval fires, oscillation.

## Why this matters for tvOS specifically

iPhone test against Pi squeezelite: ±2ms drift, server doesn't issue corrections (below 10ms threshold). Sync is bit-perfect.

tvOS test against same Pi: 13ms persistent BEHIND offset (and a separate ~127ms format-mismatch offset on track changes). Server constantly issues skipAhead, never takes effect. User reports audible echo worse than the 13ms server measurement (TV/HDMI adds processing delay invisible to AVAudioSession.outputLatency).

## Why Plan A (shrink buffer) was rejected in v1.7.9

Tried: shrink maxBufferSize from 30s to 3s + set BASS_ATTRIB_BUFFER to 200ms. Result:
- BASS_ATTRIB_BUFFER was a no-op on push streams (BASS reported back 0ms — same "not available" pattern as BASS_ChannelSetPosition per Phase 0 verification).
- 3s maxBufferSize left zero headroom for gapless track transitions; second track of an album hit pb=0KB queue=0KB at the boundary and the player choked.

Plan A reverted in same release. See ~/.claude/plans/snug-hopping-mountain.md.

## Approaches to investigate for the real fix

1. BASS DSP-based skipAhead — register a DSP via BASS_ChannelSetDSP that drops the next N samples when called by BASS. DSPs are processed at the OUTPUT layer (between BASS playback buffer and audio device), so the effect is bounded by the playback buffer (~500ms), not the push queue (~30s). Need to verify DSPs work on push streams and that "drop samples" is achievable (DSPs typically transform in-place, not skip — but BASS_ChannelGetData with DROP-style consumption may be possible).

2. Drain + re-prefix the push queue — BASS_ChannelStop + BASS_ChannelSetPosition(0) (which clears the push queue per BASS docs) + re-push the queued data starting delta further in. Disruptive (audible click/glitch on each correction), and we'd lose all queued audio. Last-resort.

3. Conditional buffer shrink — large buffer during normal playback, small buffer during sync-correction-active windows. Detect "in sync group + receiving corrections," temporarily shrink. Complex, lots of state.

4. Don't use push streams for sync — switch to URL streams (BASS_StreamCreateURL) when in a sync group. URL streams support BASS_ChannelSetPosition for instant skipAhead. Loses gapless playback (push streams are gapless, URL streams aren't). Maybe acceptable for sync-group use case.

## Files

- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:315-343 — skipAhead(duration:) sets skipAheadBytesRemaining
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1027-1041 — decoder loop discard branch (uses continue to skip BASS_StreamPutData)
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:122-130 — maxBufferSize (currently 30s for cellular resilience)
- BASS_Headers/bass.h — DSP API (BASS_ChannelSetDSP)

## Reference

- v1.7.9 release notes: LyrPlay Dev/Releases/v1.7.9.md (section "Bug 5 Investigated, dropped")
- Plan: ~/.claude/plans/snug-hopping-mountain.md
- Phase 0 verification harness: LMS_StreamTest/Phase0SyncVerification.swift (callable manually for re-verification of any new approach)

## Verification path

1. Implement chosen approach
2. Run sync test against Pi squeezelite peer with synclog at DEBUG
3. Acceptance: server-side delta converges to <10ms within 5 seconds of any artificial perturbation (format-mismatch transition, route change, etc.)
4. Manual ear test on iPhone (FLAC) and Apple TV (HDMI) for full sync session
notes:
2026-05-11: Ian replied — recommended adjusting playback rate (BASS_ATTRIB_FREQ) slightly rather than dropping data. Pointed to LIVEFX.C example. Phase 1 verification harness (Phase1FreqVerification.swift) confirmed on iPhone:
  - BASS_ATTRIB_FREQ works on push streams (readback exact, audible)
  - BASS_ChannelSlideAttribute produces smooth glissandos on push streams
  - Rate math is linear: +1% offset measured at 99.996% of expected
  - Audibility threshold: +1.0% audible, +0.5% inaudible → cap = ±0.5%

2026-05-11: /plan-eng-review locked the design. Constants: kMaxOffsetPct=0.005, kDeadbandMs=2.0, kProportionalGain=0.0005, kSlideDurationMs=200, kHardCorrectionMs=100. Hybrid path: corrections ≤100ms route through rate-match; >100ms fall through to existing byte-discard / pause/resume. 1Hz tick piggybacks on playbackHeartbeatTimer. Coordinator owns SyncController; decoder exposes setRateOffsetPct(_:). Resets at 6 sites: stream recreate, STMs, reconnect, didPauseStream, manual stop, disconnect. Default ON behind experimentalRateMatching kill switch.

2026-05-12: Implementation complete on tvos-target branch. Both iOS and tvOS targets build clean.

    EDIT: AudioStreamDecoder.swift (setRateOffsetPct/Immediate, pushStreamPositionBytes, nominalBytesPerSecond, new delegate method, callback at end of initializePushStream)

  S1 single 13ms drift converges to deadband in ~3s (acceptance: <5s) ✅
  S2 sustained 13ms/tick saturates offset at +0.5% cap, no oscillation ✅
  S3 mixed +20 / -15 cancels to +5ms residual ✅

  Self-decay math observed at 4.4ms/sec at 0.5% offset — matches theory (5ms/s ± measurement window noise).

Next: field test against Pi squeezelite peer. Watch server synclog at DEBUG, confirm delta converges <10ms within 5s of perturbation. 30-min mixed-genre ear test for any audible pitch artifacts. If clean, cleanup commit (delete Phase2SyncControllerVerification.swift + Settings button) and ship.

title: Audio dies after phone call interruption: BASS device never resumed (silent playback)
description:
## Symptom
After a phone call interruption ends, the app/UI shows playing state but produces NO audio output. CarPlay controls become unresponsive and the only fix is to kill and relaunch the app on the phone. Sometimes the app crashes instead.

## Root Cause Hypothesis (HIGH confidence)
On iOS, when AVAudioSession is interrupted by a phone call, BASS internally pauses the output device (BASS_ACTIVE_PAUSED_DEVICE state). When the interruption ends, BASS *should* auto-resume the device under default settings (BASS_IOS_SESSION_MIX is on by default), but per BASS docs: "If mixing with other apps is disabled... BASS will not automatically resume following an interruption if another app is still playing in the background. **BASS_Start can be used in that case to force resumption**."

After a phone call, the system audio session may still consider the phone app "active" briefly. BASS does not always auto-resume the device. The result: BASS_ChannelPlay() returns success (channel is "playing") but the device is paused, so no audio reaches the speaker.

The dev already discovered this for route changes — see AudioManager.swift:146-150 (manual-skip path) which explicitly calls `BASS_Start()` with comment "After route change, BASS device may be paused (BASS_ACTIVE_PAUSED_DEVICE)".

But the interruption-resume path does NOT call BASS_Start():
- `PlaybackSessionController.handleInterruption(.ended)` → sends server "play" command
- Server → `didResumeStream()` → `audioManager.play()` → `streamDecoder.resumePlayback()`
- `resumePlayback()` only calls `BASS_ChannelPlay(pushStream, 0)` — NO `BASS_Start()`

## Why Intermittent
- Brief phone calls (<45s background): code path `sendLockScreenCommand("play")` just sends play, never recreates stream → resumePlayback() path → bug hits
- Long calls (>45s background): triggers full recovery via playlist jump → didStartPushStream → startPushStreamPlayback() which DOES call BASS_Start() → works
- BASS sometimes auto-resumes correctly depending on whether iOS considers "another app still playing"

## Proposed Fix
Add `BASS_Start()` call before `BASS_ChannelPlay()` in `AudioStreamDecoder.resumePlayback()` (line 518) and possibly in `AudioPlayer.play()` resume paths. Same pattern as AudioManager.swift:149.

## Verification Path
1. Add temporary log in resumePlayback() that calls BASS_IsStarted() and BASS_ChannelIsActive() BEFORE BASS_ChannelPlay
2. Reproduce by calling phone (or use Siri) while music is playing
3. Confirm hypothesis: BASS_IsStarted() returns 0 (FALSE) post-interruption
4. Apply fix and verify audio resumes

## Files
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:494-525 (pause/resume push stream)
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioPlayer.swift:340-395 (URL stream resume)
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioManager.swift:146-150 (existing BASS_Start example)
- LMS_StreamTest/PlaybackSessionController.swift:331-392 (interruption handling)
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:947-966 (didResumeStream)

## References
- docs/bass_documentation/BASS_CONFIG_IOS_SESSION.html: "BASS_Start can be used... to force resumption"
- docs/bass_documentation/BASS_Start.html

title: Gapless playback: server UI and CarPlay jump to next track ~30s early (2/10 tracks)
description:
## Bug
During gapless album playback, server interface and CarPlay switch to next track metadata/time before current track finishes playing (~30s early). Self-corrects when audio catches up. Intermittent ~2/10 transitions.

## Reproduction
1. Play album (app always in gapless mode)
2. Near end of track A, server UI switches to track B (metadata changes, time=0:00, holds)
3. Player still audibly playing track A (~30s remaining)
4. When track A finishes, track B starts and server timer begins progressing

## Investigation (2026-04-02)

### Gapless flow traced:
1. Track A decoder finishes → STMd sent → server queues track B (sends STRM)
2. Server UI advances to track B immediately (shows 0:00)
3. New decoder starts for track B, first chunk marks boundary in push stream
4. BASS_SYNC_POS callback fires at boundary → STMs sent → server timer starts

### Root cause hypothesis (unconfirmed):
Decoder throttle in AudioStreamDecoder.swift line 862 only checks BASS_ChannelGetData(BASS_DATA_AVAILABLE) which is the playback buffer. Does NOT include the push stream queue (BASS_StreamPutData(nil,0)). Queue grows unbounded (up to 600MB limit) while throttle never triggers.

### Why intermittent (unknown):
If throttle is truly broken, should happen 10/10 not 2/10. Need field data to confirm. Possible explanations: BASS_DATA_AVAILABLE might include queue sometimes, or other backpressure exists.

### Key code paths:
- Throttle: AudioStreamDecoder.swift:862 (maxBufferSize=705600 ~2s)
- STMd: SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:987 (sendTrackDecodeComplete)
- Boundary mark: AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1229 (markTrackBoundary)
- STMs: SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1015 (sendTrackStarted)
- Server time poll: SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1195 (fetchServerTime, every 3s)

## Diagnostics (v1.7.7, branch fix/gapless-carplay-premature-update)
GaplessDiagnostics.swift — ring buffer auto-captures every gapless transition with buffer breakdown (playback vs queue). Export via Settings > Copy Gapless Log.

### What the diagnostic data will tell us:
1. Exact playback buffer vs queue sizes at STMd — proves/disproves throttle theory
2. Time gap between STMd and STMs — confirms ~30s report
3. Whether 2/10 tracks have different buffer characteristics than 8/10

## Status
Awaiting field diagnostic data from drive session.
notes:
## Update 2026-04-03: Root cause confirmed, fix implemented

### Diagnostic data collected
First field test (v1.7.7 diagnostics build) confirmed:
- Queue at STMd: 85,583 KB (83.6 MB) — 228 seconds of audio buffered
- Playback buffer: only 188 KB (throttle target was 705 KB, never triggered)
- STMs fired 42 seconds early (predicted ETA 228.3s, actual 186.8s)
- Old predicted boundary position was 59 MB (154 seconds!) off from correct position

### Root cause: two bugs

**Bug 1 — Boundary prediction drift (fixed in 5eab14b):**
markTrackBoundary() calculated boundary = playbackPos + playbackBuffer + queue by sampling 3 non-atomic BASS APIs. With 85MB queue, measurement error drifted ~42s. Fix: use totalBytesPushed directly — our equivalent of squeezelite's output.track_start = outputbuf->writep. This is the exact byte offset stamped at decode time. BASS_SYNC_POS fires when playback position reaches it. Zero prediction needed.

**Bug 2 — Throttle not checking queue (fixed in 9d7aca4):**
Decoder throttle only checked BASS_ChannelGetData(BASS_DATA_AVAILABLE) = playback buffer (~188KB). Never saw the push queue (85MB+). Entire track decoded into queue instantly. Fix: check playback + queue combined, target 30 seconds (~11.5MB) for cellular dead spot resilience. BASS hard limit lowered from 600MB to 50MB.

### Protocol understanding corrected
Server updates Material UI metadata at STMs (track started), NOT at STMd (decode complete). So the premature UI switch was caused by our early STMs, not inherent server behavior. The boundary fix directly addresses the user-visible bug.

### Status
Both fixes committed on branch fix/gapless-carplay-premature-update. Awaiting field validation with next test drive.

title: Fix premature track skipping due to network hiccups
description:
## Root Cause Analysis

GitHub issue #64 - Users report intermittent track skipping mid-playback.

### The Problem

AudioStreamDecoder.swift (lines 884-886, 930-932) triggers track completion when:
1. `bytesRead == 0` or `BASS_ERROR_ENDED` (no more frames to decode)
2. `BASS_StreamGetFilePosition(..., BASS_FILEPOS_CONNECTED) == 0` (HTTP disconnected)

This follows squeezelite's pattern:
```c
if (n == 0 && stream.state <= DISCONNECT) return DECODE_COMPLETE;
```

**However**, squeezelite has explicit disconnect reason codes:
- `DISCONNECT_OK = 0` - Server closed properly (track really ended)
- `LOCAL_DISCONNECT = 1` - Local error
- `REMOTE_DISCONNECT = 2` - Remote error
- `UNREACHABLE = 3` - Connection failure
- `TIMEOUT = 4` - Timeout

STMd is only sent when `stream.disconnect == DISCONNECT_OK` (slimproto.c:671).

**BASS has no such distinction**. `BASS_FILEPOS_CONNECTED == 0` doesn't tell us WHY the connection dropped.

### Why Radio Streams Work

Radio streams are continuous - they don't trigger track completion logic. The decoder loop keeps running, waiting for more data.

### Proposed Fix

**Option 1: Duration Validation**
Pass expected track duration from STRM command. Before sending STMd, verify:
```swift
let decodedDuration = Double(totalBytesPushed) / Double(sampleRate * channels * 4)
if decodedDuration < expectedDuration * 0.9 {  // < 90% decoded
    os_log(.warning, "Premature disconnect - network error, not track end")
    // Don't send STMd - either retry or wait
    return
}
```

**Option 2: File Size Validation**
Use `BASS_FILEPOS_SIZE` (Content-Length) and `BASS_FILEPOS_END` (downloaded bytes):
```swift
let expectedSize = BASS_StreamGetFilePosition(stream, DWORD(BASS_FILEPOS_SIZE))
let downloadedSize = BASS_StreamGetFilePosition(stream, DWORD(BASS_FILEPOS_END))
if expectedSize > 0 && downloadedSize < expectedSize {
    // Incomplete download - network error
    return
}
```

**Option 3: Reconnection with Buffer**
When disconnect detected with buffer remaining:
1. Don't immediately declare track complete
2. Wait brief period (1-2s) for connection recovery
3. Only send STMd if reconnection fails AND buffer drains

### Files to Modify
- AudioStreamDecoder.swift: Add validation before audioStreamDecoderDidCompleteTrack()
- SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift: Pass expected duration to decoder

### Related Issues
- LMS_StreamTest-6lb: Reconnection position jumps (different issue - post-reconnect, not during disconnect)
- This is the original gapless implementation (e45a8689) missing squeezelite's DISCONNECT_OK distinction

title: CarPlay shows next track metadata prematurely after playlist jump recovery
description:
## Updated Root Cause Analysis (Jan 24, 2026)

**Previous hypothesis was WRONG.** Server time filtering doesn't fix the issue.

### Actual Root Cause: BASS Sync Callback Fires Early

Testing revealed that with ~30s left in Track A:
1. Track B artwork appears
2. Timer resets to 0 and counts UP (not cycling like before)

This means `sendTrackStarted()` is being called ~30s before Track A ends:
- Sends STMs to server (telling server we're on Track B)
- Resets SimpleTimeTracker to 0
- Fetches metadata (correctly returns Track B since we just told server we switched)

**We're lying to the server by sending STMs too early, not the other way around!**

### The Problem Chain

1. `markTrackBoundary()` calculates boundary position:
   ```swift
   trackBoundaryPosition = playbackPos + totalBuffered
   ```

2. BASS sync callback is registered for this position

3. If `totalBuffered` is larger than expected (or calculation is wrong), callback fires early

4. `handleTrackBoundary()` → `sendTrackStarted()` → sends STMs + resets time + fetches metadata

### Why Intermittent?

Buffer sizes vary based on:
- Network conditions during Opus transcoding
- Timing of when boundary is marked
- BASS internal buffering state

### Next Steps

1. Add logging to `markTrackBoundary()` to capture actual values
2. Add logging to `handleTrackBoundary()` to see when callback fires
3. Compare expected vs actual track end timing
4. Check if boundary calculation formula is correct

### Key Files

- `AudioStreamDecoder.swift`: `markTrackBoundary()` (line ~1229), `handleTrackBoundary()` (line ~1321)
- `SlimProtoCoordinator.swift`: `sendTrackStarted()` (line ~1018)

comments.author: Your Name
comments.text:
## Investigation Complete - Fix Applied (Jan 23, 2026)

### BASS Documentation Review

Reviewed official BASS documentation for push stream buffer functions:

**BASS_StreamPutData(nil, 0):**
- Returns 'the amount of data currently queued'
- Queue = overflow waiting for playback buffer space

**BASS_ChannelGetData(nil, BASS_DATA_AVAILABLE):**
- Returns 'the amount of data the channel has buffered for playback'
- This is the internal playback buffer (~500ms default)

**These are DIFFERENT buffers** - data flows: Push Queue → Playback Buffer → Output

### Root Cause Identified

The old calculation was:
```swift
trackBoundaryPosition = playbackPos + playbackBuffered + queuedAmount
```

This SHOULD equal `totalBytesPushed` (our write position), but may not for push streams due to:
1. Timing between reading multiple BASS values
2. Possible double-counting if buffers overlap
3. Internal BASS buffering not fully exposed

### Fix Applied

Changed to squeezelite-style approach using write position directly:
```swift
trackBoundaryPosition = totalBytesPushed
```

This is simpler and matches squeezelite's `output.track_start = outputbuf->writep`.

Added diagnostic logging to compare both calculations - if they differ, we'll know exactly what's wrong.

### Files Modified

- `AudioStreamDecoder.swift`: `markTrackBoundary()` - uses write position, logs comparison

## Fix Verified - Cleanup Complete (Jan 24, 2026)

### Testing Results

Boundary timing is now **SAMPLE-PERFECT**:
```
Playback position: 71851608 bytes (187.11 seconds)
Expected boundary: 71851584 bytes (187.11 seconds)  
Timing accuracy: 24 bytes difference (0.000 seconds)
```

24 bytes = 0.00006 seconds = essentially perfect!

### Final Changes

1. **AudioStreamDecoder.swift** - `markTrackBoundary()`:
   - Changed to use `totalBytesPushed` (write position) as boundary
   - Matches squeezelite's `output.track_start = outputbuf->writep`
   - Added diagnostic logging comparing both calculation methods

2. **SlimProtoCoordinator.swift** - Removed `isGaplessBufferingPending` flag:
   - Removed property declaration
   - Removed setting/clearing logic
   - Removed server time filtering during gapless buffering
   - This filtering was unnecessary since the real fix was in boundary calculation

### Root Cause Summary

The BASS sync callback was being set at the wrong position. The old calculation:
```swift
boundary = playbackPos + playbackBuffer + queueBuffer
```

Was replaced with:
```swift
boundary = totalBytesPushed  // Our write position
```

Both calculations produce the same value (verified in testing), but using the write position directly is simpler and more reliable.

title: iPad: WebView layout compressed after app minimize/restore (iOS 26)
description:
## Problem

On iPad only (iOS 26), after minimizing the app and reopening, the WKWebView becomes horizontally compressed to roughly half the screen width. The content appears squished to the left with black/empty space on the right.

**Workaround:** Rotating the device fixes the layout.

## Root Cause Analysis

The `WebView` UIViewRepresentable's `updateUIView` function only checks for URL host changes - it doesn't handle layout updates after app state changes:

```swift
func updateUIView(_ uiView: WKWebView, context: Context) {
    // ADD THIS - check if host changed:
    if let currentURL = uiView.url, currentURL.host != url.host {
        let request = URLRequest(url: url, cachePolicy: .reloadIgnoringLocalAndRemoteCacheData)
        uiView.load(request)
    }
    // ❌ NO LAYOUT HANDLING
}
```

When iPad returns from background/multitasking, the WebView's frame may not be updated correctly. iOS 26 may have new multitasking behavior that exacerbates this.

## Proposed Fixes

### Fix 1: Force layout in updateUIView (Simplest)
```swift
func updateUIView(_ uiView: WKWebView, context: Context) {
    // Force layout update on every SwiftUI update cycle
    uiView.setNeedsLayout()
    uiView.layoutIfNeeded()
    
    // Existing host change check...
}
```

### Fix 2: Use GeometryReader to detect size changes
```swift
GeometryReader { geometry in
    WebView(url: url, size: geometry.size, ...)
}

// Then in WebView:
func updateUIView(_ uiView: WKWebView, context: Context) {
    uiView.frame = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)
}
```

### Fix 3: Listen for sceneDidBecomeActive
```swift
func makeUIView(context: Context) -> WKWebView {
    // ... existing code ...
    
    NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
        forName: UIScene.didActivateNotification,
        object: nil,
        queue: .main
    ) { _ in
        webView.setNeedsLayout()
        webView.layoutIfNeeded()
    }
    
    return webView
}
```

### Fix 4: Override viewportFit or scrollView behavior
The WebView has these settings that might interact badly with iPad multitasking:
```swift
webView.scrollView.contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior = .never
webView.scrollView.automaticallyAdjustsScrollIndicatorInsets = false
```

Try changing to:
```swift
webView.scrollView.contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior = .automatic
```

## Files to Modify
- **ContentView.swift**: WebView struct, updateUIView function

## Testing
1. Open app on iPad in landscape
2. Minimize app (swipe up)
3. Reopen app
4. Verify WebView fills full width
5. Test in portrait orientation too
6. Test with Split View multitasking

## References
- iOS 26 may have new window scene behavior
- Similar issues reported with WKWebView and iPad multitasking
- Rotation fixing it confirms it's a layout/frame issue
notes:
## Research Findings

This is a **long-standing WebKit bug** (since iOS 10.3):

### WebKit Bug 170595
`window.innerWidth/innerHeight` return **wrong values** during resize/orientation events in WKWebView. Material skin uses these to calculate layout, so it gets stale dimensions after app backgrounding/foregrounding.

### References
- [WebKit Bug 170595](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=170595) - window.innerWidth/innerHeight bogus after resize
- [Cordova iOS Issue #933](https://github.com/apache/cordova-ios/issues/933) - WKWebView reports wrong size
- [iOS 18 WebKit fix](https://www.mail-archive.com/webkit-changes@lists.webkit.org/msg216753.html) - Related orientation issue

### Known Workarounds
| Workaround | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| **Delay** | Wait 500-700ms before reading dimensions |
| **Polling** | Check dimensions repeatedly until stable |
| **getBoundingClientRect()** | Use on a full-window element instead |
| **clientWidth/clientHeight** | Use `document.documentElement.clientWidth` instead |
| **Force reflow** | Toggle display:none to force layout recalc |

## Fix Attempts

### Attempt 1: setNeedsLayout (FAILED)
Added to `updateUIView`:
```swift
uiView.setNeedsLayout()
uiView.layoutIfNeeded()
```
**Result:** Did not fix - issue is in web content JS, not native view frame.

### Attempt 2: Immediate resize event (FAILED)
```javascript
window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'));
```
**Result:** Did not fix - WebKit still reports wrong dimensions immediately.

### Attempt 3: Delayed resize event (TESTING)
```javascript
setTimeout(function() { window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')); }, 500);
```
**Rationale:** 500ms delay lets WebKit settle before Material recalculates.

## Other Options to Try
1. **Longer delay** (700ms)
2. **Force reflow via JS:**
```javascript
document.body.style.display = 'none';
document.body.offsetHeight;
document.body.style.display = '';
```
3. **Dispatch orientationchange event instead**
4. **Multiple delayed resize events** (500ms, 1000ms)

title: Fix reconnection position jumps with continuous position tracking
description:
## Problem

When LyrPlay loses connection (e.g., cellular dropout) while playing from buffer:
1. Audio continues playing from buffer (can be 2 songs worth)
2. Network restores → auto-reconnect triggers
3. Server sends STRM at stale position (last STMt before disconnect)
4. User experiences backward position jump or wrong track

Root cause: Server's last known position becomes stale while client plays from buffer.

## Solution: Continuous Position Tracking + Playlist Jump on Reconnect

### Part 1: Always Save Position (Periodic)

Piggyback on existing `serverTimeTimer` (3 second interval):

```swift
// In fetchServerTime() or nearby
if audioManager.streamDecoder.isPlaying() || audioManager.streamDecoder.hasValidStream() {
    let position = audioManager.streamDecoder.getCurrentPosition()
    if position > 0 {
        UserDefaults.standard.set(position, forKey: "lyrplay_recovery_position")
    }
}
```

### Part 2: Track Index on Boundary (Offline-Safe)

When gapless track boundary crossed, increment saved index:

```swift
// In sendTrackBoundaryNotification() or AudioManager delegate callback
let currentIndex = UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: "lyrplay_recovery_index")
UserDefaults.standard.set(currentIndex + 1, forKey: "lyrplay_recovery_index")
```

This works even when disconnected because boundary callback fires from BASS.

### Part 3: Sync Index When Connected

When server provides authoritative playlist_cur_index, update local:

```swift
// In fetchServerTime() response, fetchCurrentMetadata(), or status parsing
if let serverIndex = result["playlist_cur_index"] as? Int {
    UserDefaults.standard.set(serverIndex, forKey: "lyrplay_recovery_index")
}
```

### Part 4: Playlist Jump on Reconnect

In `slimProtoDidConnect()`, always do playlist jump recovery:

```swift
func slimProtoDidConnect() {
    // ... existing code ...
    
    // CRITICAL: Override server auto-resume with our accurate position
    // Server's position is stale if we played from buffer while disconnected
    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.0) {
        self.performPlaylistRecovery(shouldPlay: true)
    }
}
```

### Part 5: Avoid Conflicts with Lock Screen Recovery

Lock screen recovery already calls performPlaylistRecovery(). Need to ensure:
- `isRecoveryInProgress` flag prevents double-recovery
- Or: unify all reconnect paths through single recovery mechanism

## Files to Modify

- **SlimProtoCoordinator.swift**:
  - Add position saving in fetchServerTime() 
  - Add playlist jump in slimProtoDidConnect()
  - Add index sync when server provides playlist_cur_index
  - Increment index in sendTrackBoundaryNotification()

- **AudioManager.swift** (optional):
  - May need to expose decoder state more cleanly

## Testing Scenarios

1. **Same track recovery**: Disconnect at 1:30, buffer plays to 3:00, reconnect → should resume at 3:00
2. **Gapless transition**: Disconnect at track 5, 3:00 → buffer plays through to track 6, 1:00 → reconnect at track 6, 1:00  
3. **Quick reconnect**: Disconnect/reconnect within 5 seconds → should work normally
4. **Lock screen + disconnect**: Ensure no conflict between lock screen recovery and reconnect recovery
5. **Manual skip after reconnect**: Ensure index syncs correctly from server

## Related

- Closes issue LMS_StreamTest-d98 (backward jumps and track skips on reconnect)
- Replaces complex reconnect bit approach with simpler continuous tracking
notes:
## Reconnection & Recovery Flow Documentation

### 1. What Triggers Automatic Reconnect

**SlimProtoConnectionManager** handles reconnection:

| Trigger | Code Path |
|---------|-----------|
| **Network restored** | `networkPathUpdateHandler` → `attemptReconnection()` |
| **App becomes active** | `appDidBecomeActive()` → `attemptReconnection()` |
| **Health check fails** | `handleHealthCheckFailure()` → `attemptReconnection()` |
| **Connection lost** | `didDisconnect()` → `scheduleReconnection()` |

**The actual reconnect:**
```
attemptReconnection() 
  → delegate?.connectionManagerShouldReconnect()
  → SlimProtoCoordinator.connectionManagerShouldReconnect()
  → sets pendingRecoveryTrigger = .networkRestored
  → connect()
```

### 2. How Playlist Jump is Triggered

When connection succeeds:
```
slimProtoDidConnect()
  → handlePendingRecovery()
  → checks pendingRecoveryTrigger
  → performPlaylistRecovery(shouldPlay: true/false)
```

**Three recovery triggers:**

| Trigger | When Set | Recovery Behavior |
|---------|----------|-------------------|
| `.networkRestored` | Auto-reconnect after disconnect | Resume previous state (play if was playing) |
| `.lockScreen` | User presses play on lock screen after >45s background | Play with position recovery |
| `.appOpen` | App opened after background disconnect | Muted + paused (silent recovery) |

### 3. The Actual Playlist Jump Command

```swift
// performPlaylistRecovery() sends:
["playlist", "jump", savedIndex, 1, 0, ["timeOffset": savedPosition]]
```

- Reads `savedIndex` and `savedPosition` from UserDefaults
- Jumps to correct track at correct position
- `shouldPlay` determines if it starts playing or stays paused

### 4. Visual Flow
```
[Network Lost]
     ↓
slimProtoDidDisconnect() → saves wasPlayingBeforeDisconnect
     ↓
[Audio continues from buffer, NowPlayingManager saves position every 1s]
     ↓
[Network Restored]
     ↓
connectionManagerShouldReconnect() → pendingRecoveryTrigger = .networkRestored
     ↓
connect() → HELO handshake
     ↓
slimProtoDidConnect() → handlePendingRecovery()
     ↓
performPlaylistRecovery(shouldPlay: wasPlayingBeforeDisconnect)
     ↓
[Playlist jump command sent to server with saved position]
```

### 5. Position Saving Architecture (Fixed)

| Component | Timer | Never Stops | Saves Position |
|-----------|-------|-------------|----------------|
| NowPlayingManager | updateTimer (1s) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| SlimProtoCoordinator | playbackHeartbeatTimer (1s) | ❌ Stops on disconnect | ❌ No (removed) |
| SlimProtoCoordinator | serverTimeTimer (3s) | ❌ Stops on disconnect | ❌ No (removed) |

**Key insight:** NowPlayingManager's timer never stops, so position continues to be saved even while disconnected and playing from buffer.
close_reason: Implemented as unified recovery architecture (PR #61 feature/unified-recovery-6lb): periodic position save + playlist jump on reconnect is the shipped design.

title: Change default audio format from .compressed to .flac for fresh installs
description:
## Current Code

**SettingsManager.swift:206**
```swift
let audioFormatRaw = UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: Keys.audioFormat)
audioFormat = AudioFormat(rawValue: audioFormatRaw) ?? .compressed
```

**Current default**: `.compressed` (MP3 preferred)
**Desired default**: `.flac` (Lossless FLAC)

## AudioFormat Enum Values

```swift
enum AudioFormat: Int {
    case compressed = 0    // ← Current default
    case aacPreferred = 1
    case oggVorbis = 2
    case flac = 3          // ← Desired default
    case opus = 4
    case custom = 5
}
```

## Problem

Fresh installs default to `.compressed` which prioritizes MP3/AAC over FLAC:
- **compressed**: `"mp3,aac"` capability codes
- **flac**: `"flc,ops,ogg,alc,aac,mp3"` capability codes

Users with high-quality FLAC libraries get MP3 transcodes by default.

## Solution

Change line 206 from:
```swift
audioFormat = AudioFormat(rawValue: audioFormatRaw) ?? .compressed
```

To:
```swift
audioFormat = AudioFormat(rawValue: audioFormatRaw) ?? .flac
```

## Migration Impact

**Fresh installs**: Get FLAC-first format priority ✅
**Existing users**: Keep their saved audioFormat setting ✅

UserDefaults will have `audioFormat` key already set, so fallback never triggers for existing users.

## Files to Modify

- **SettingsManager.swift**: Line 206 only

## Testing

1. **Fresh install**: Delete app, install, verify Settings shows "Lossless (FLAC)" by default
2. **Existing user**: Upgrade from old build, verify format setting preserved
3. **Capability string**: Verify HELO message includes `flc,ops,ogg,alc,aac,mp3`

## Rationale

LyrPlay positions as premium/high-quality audio app. Users expect best quality out of box. Mobile transcode toggle already exists for data optimization.

## Priority

P1 - Better first impression, matches app positioning
