title: Format-mismatch deferred-track-start doesn't use synchronized start — sync drops on format change
description:
## Problem

When a track's audio format (sample rate or channel count) differs from the currently playing track, AudioStreamDecoder destroys the existing BASS push stream and creates a new one (the "deferred track start" / "format mismatch" code path). This recreation takes ~100ms and **does not use the server's synchronized-start mechanism (strm 'u' jiffies)** — the new stream just plays as soon as it's ready.

Result: in a multi-room sync group, the player drifts behind peers by the stream-recreation overhead each time format changes mid-playlist. Observed on tvOS test 2026-05-09: track 2 started ~127ms behind the Raspberry Pi squeezelite peer because it was a different format than track 1.

## Why other players don't have this problem

Hardware Squeezeboxes and squeezelite reconfigure their existing audio output for the new format without destroying and recreating the stream. Audio is contiguous; sync continues seamlessly.

LyrPlay's BASS push stream is bound to a fixed sample rate and channel count at creation. There's no "reconfigure rate mid-stream" API on push streams. Free + recreate is the current path.

## Relationship to LMS_StreamTest-b5o (skipAhead delay)

If b5o is fixed (skipAhead actually works), this bug becomes self-healing: server detects the ~127ms initial offset, sends skipAhead 127ms, player skips, sync restored within 1-2 seconds. Without b5o fixed, the format-mismatch initial offset persists indefinitely (server keeps issuing the correction but the buffer-delay prevents it from taking effect).

This bug should be addressed BUT b5o is the higher-leverage fix.

## Approaches

1. Use sync-start for the new stream — when destroying+recreating the push stream during a format-mismatch transition, request the server's strm 'u' jiffies-target before starting playback on the new stream. Requires server cooperation (does the server send strm 'u' for mid-playlist format changes? need to verify).

2. Avoid the destroy-recreate cycle — investigate whether BASS supports any way to reconfigure a push stream's sample rate / channel count without recreation. Probably not (push streams are immutable in format), but worth checking.

3. Pre-create the new stream before the boundary — start the new push stream during the previous track's tail, sync-start it, swap the active stream at the boundary. Adds complexity but eliminates the ~100ms recreation gap.

4. Accept and let b5o fix it — once skipAhead works, this is self-correcting within 1-2 seconds. May be acceptable to defer indefinitely.

## Files

- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:780-800 — format-mismatch destroy+recreate (in startPushStreamPlayback)
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1480-1500 — same pattern in [APP-RECOVERY] deferred-track path
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:474-530 — handleUnpauseCommand + sync start routing (the existing sync-start path that works for first track)

## Reference

- v1.7.9 release notes: LyrPlay Dev/Releases/v1.7.9.md
- Linked issue: LMS_StreamTest-b5o (root cause of inability to recover)

title: tvOS Settings v1 — gear on Now Playing + 4-section List
description:
Add a tvOS Settings screen for v1 TestFlight cut, addressing the post-bia
UX gap: a connected user has no in-app path to change LMS server, rename
the player, or pick a different audio format.

Design doc: ~/.gstack/projects/LMS_StreamTest/ericmiller-tvos-target-design-20260507-121432.md
Status: APPROVED (2 rounds /office-hours adversarial review, 9/10).

## Locked decisions

- D1 — Modest scope: Server / Player Name / Audio Format / About
- D2 — Server change reuses ServerConnectView (no new entry UI)
- D3 — Single-screen List with inline controls (avoids 98q-9bb push-hides-tabbar)
- D4 — Lateral placement: gear on NowPlayingView, NOT a 4th tab. TabView stays at 3 content tabs (Now Playing / Search / Library)
- D5 — Gear top-right of NowPlayingView, always visible regardless of track state (works when server unreachable)

## Implementation order (per design doc)

1. SettingsView.swift (new, tvOS-only) — wraps NavigationStack so sub-screens (Server Change) push WITHIN the cover. Root is a 4-section List.
2. Wire gear into NowPlayingView — own .focusSection() outside artwork's section so it doesn't compete with artwork-tap-for-visualizer (98q.7). .prefersDefaultFocus(in:) on playback panel preserves 98q.5 default.
3. Server change — ServerConnectView pushed via NavigationStack (NOT nested fullScreenCover). On confirm: attempt connect to new host BEFORE writing settings. On success: clear lyrplay_recovery_index + lyrplay_recovery_position UserDefaults keys (saved index points to OLD server's playlist — CLAUDE.md rule #4 atomicity), write new host, tear down + rebuild SlimProtoCoordinator as fresh connect, dismiss cover. On failure: keep old host, surface error in ServerConnectView.
4. Player name — two-way bind to settings.playerName. Re-HELO on next reconnect (deferred, not urgent).
5. Audio format — Picker bound to settings.preferredAudioFormat. Verify inline rendering on tvOS; if it auto-pushes a detail screen, that's acceptable (uses the cover's NavigationStack from step 1).
6. About section — non-focusable HStack(label, value) rows: version (CFBundleShortVersionString), build (CFBundleVersion), server host, player MAC. .focusable(false) so focus skips them.
7. Hardware verification on Apple TV 4K — all 4 sections + server-change roundtrip + bad-IP failure path + gear focus reachability from each tab.

## Success criteria

- Server change works without uninstall, with bad-IP failure preserving old config
- Player name editable without reinstall
- Audio format change applies to next track (non-disruptive)
- Settings reachable in ≤4 button presses from any tab
- Opening Settings during playback does not interrupt audio
- VoiceOver announces gear as "Settings", reads About rows label-then-value
- No regression to TabView strip, focus engine, or HW play/pause from -bia

## Blocks
LMS_StreamTest-kua (TestFlight v1 beta)

## Reuses
ServerConnectView, SettingsManager, SlimProtoCoordinator reset path, fullScreenCover pattern (Queue + Visualizer), MediaRow shape if adapted for About rows.

## Out of scope
Log export, debug toggles, separate "reset to onboarding" affordance, copy-to-clipboard on About rows, one-time discoverability tooltip. Defer to v2 polish based on TestFlight feedback.

title: tvOS audio session interruption handling (Siri / AirPlay / route changes)
description:
Deferred from -bia v1 fix (commits c565627 + e9fc605 on tvos-target, 2026-05-07).

## Scope

Listen to AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification on tvOS and coordinate pause/resume with the LMS server. Currently the tvOS target has no equivalent of iOS PlaybackSessionController.

## Why deferred (not v1)

The -bia fix landed AVAudioSession activation + UIBackgroundModes. Audio playback now survives home-screen press. But interruption events (Siri activation, AirPlay route change to/from Apple TV, screensaver in some setups) are not handled — audio may stall after interruption without proper begin/end notifications.

Per /plan-eng-review 2026-05-07 D4: deferred because:
1. Adds a new subsystem (state coordination, BASS interaction, hardware testing across all interruption types), not marginal effort.
2. tvOS interruption events are rare in normal usage (no phone calls, no notification-triggered audio).
3. -bia hardware-verification did not surface user-visible interruption breakage.

## Plan

Two implementation choices:
- A) Extend PlaybackSessionController (iOS-only currently) with #if-guarded tvOS branches.
- B) Create tvOSPlaybackSessionController as a parallel file (Group C pattern).

iOS PlaybackSessionController has heavy iOS-specific surface (CarPlay command center, route change handlers, pause-on-call). Counting actually-needed sites for tvOS will determine A vs B (per audit-overcounts-ios-coupling pattern).

## Reference

iOS PlaybackSessionController.swift handleInterruption(_:) is the model. Apple docs: AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification.

## Test surface

Hardware-only:
- Siri activation while playing → audio ducks/pauses → Siri ends → audio resumes
- AirPlay route change away from Apple TV → audio stops cleanly → route returns → audio resumes
- Screensaver activation while playing → audio continues (UIBackgroundModes audio)

## Blocked

Not blocked. Lower priority than -kua TestFlight cut.

title: tvOS: Radio stream artwork not populating in Now Playing (works on iOS)
description:

1. Tap a radio favorite in tvOS Library → Favorites (e.g., Radio Paradise — `radioparadise://4-1.flac`)
2. Track + artist update in Now Playing (good)
3. Cover art remains placeholder (BUG — should show RP's per-song album art)

iOS shows artwork for the same favorite via Material WebView.

## Diagnostic context

**Not a 98q.9 regression.** Phases 1-4 of 98q.9 did not touch:
- `LMS_StreamTest/NowPlayingManager.swift` (currentArtwork, loadArtwork)
- `LMS_StreamTest/AudioManager.swift` (updateTrackMetadata pass-through)
- `LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift` (fetchCurrentTrackMetadata, handleICYMetadata)
- `LMS_StreamTest/AudioPlayer.swift` (ICY callback wiring)
- `LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/NowPlayingView.swift` (artworkPanel rendering)

This is a pre-existing tvOS gap from 98q.5 (Now Playing) that wasn't caught because manual hardware tests focused on local-library tracks (which always have valid coverid).

## Likely root cause (to verify)

Radio metadata in LMS flows two ways:

1. **Initial play** — `fetchCurrentTrackMetadata()` fires 500ms after STMs (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1085-1089). Reads `firstTrack["artwork_url"]` then `firstTrack["coverid"]` (lines 1962-1967). For radio:
   - RadioParadise has an LMS plugin that publishes per-track `artwork_url` to the now-playing track in `playlist_loop[0]`.
   - If that plugin path returns nothing or different field, our reader gets nil → currentArtwork=nil.

2. **Track changes within stream** — BASS_TAG_META callback fires (`AudioPlayer.swift:954`), routes to `handleICYMetadata` (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:243). That handler ONLY pushes title/artist to LMS via `["icy", ...]` — it does NOT trigger a local re-fetch. So when a new song comes on the radio, our local `currentArtwork` isn't updated unless something ELSE (server push? subscribe?) triggers fetchCurrentTrackMetadata.

iOS may be unaffected because:
- Material WebView (iOS-only) has its own metadata pipeline independent of NowPlayingManager.
- iOS lock screen Now Playing may also be missing radio art today and we just didn't notice.

## Investigation steps

1. While Radio Paradise is playing on tvOS, probe LMS at `192.168.1.8:9000/jsonrpc.js` with `["status", "-", 1, "tags:K"]` (or the same call our coordinator makes — see `fetchCurrentTrackMetadata` body) using the player's MAC. Check if `artwork_url` or `coverid` is populated for the current radio track. If yes → our reader is broken. If no → server-side plugin gap.

2. While playing, watch console for `🖼️ Loading artwork from:` logs (NowPlayingManager.swift:275). If absent → URL never built. If present but `❌ Failed to load artwork` → fetch error (HTTP, auth, CORS).

3. Verify iOS lock screen (NOT Material UI) actually shows radio art. If iOS lock screen is also missing it, then this is a feature gap not a tvOS-only regression.

4. Listen for ICY metadata callbacks fired during playback (`🎵 New ICY metadata` log in SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:253). Each one currently only sends title/artist to LMS — it does NOT update local artwork. Consider: after sending ICY to LMS, fetch fresh metadata to pick up new artwork URL.

## Out of 98q.9 scope

This is Now Playing tab work, separate from Library tab. Filed as P2 since it materially degrades the radio listening experience but doesn't block 98q.9 acceptance (Library tab functions for tap-to-play and LMS-library tracks render artwork correctly).

## Possible fixes (do not implement until investigated)

A. After `handleICYMetadata` sends to LMS, schedule `fetchCurrentTrackMetadata()` 200-500ms later to pull updated artwork.
B. Subscribe to LMS push notifications for currentsong changes (different mechanism, larger change).
C. Check if RadioParadise plugin populates `coverid` differently than expected (server-side).

## Affected files (read, not edit, until cause confirmed)
- `LMS_StreamTest/NowPlayingManager.swift:264-271` (loadArtwork trigger)
- `LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:243-303` (handleICYMetadata + sendICYMetadataToLMS)
- `LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1881-2010` (fetchCurrentTrackMetadata + artwork URL build)
acceptance_criteria: Radio favorites display per-track album art in tvOS Now Playing for streams with metadata-feed support (RadioParadise, BBC, etc). Verified on Apple TV hardware with at least 2 different streaming sources.
close_reason: Fixed via radio metadata refresh timer (57d0abd, 61b5238); radio artwork field-verified in a7r work (build 33/20).

comments.author: mtxmiller
comments.text: Pilot triage: likely fixed in 57d0abd ('Add radio metadata refresh timer (real fix for -2tc)') + 61b5238 + 6990893. Recommend verify & close.

title: tvOS: hierarchical Favorites browsing (folders)
description:
## Context (deferred from 98q.9 plan-eng-review, 2026-05-06)

98q.9 (Favorites + Recently Played) shipped with **flat-flat Favorites** — only items with playable URLs are rendered; folder items (`hasitems:1`, no direct url) are filtered out. This was D3 in plan-eng-review.

For users with folder-organized favorites (LMS Apps like Spotty, BBC Sounds, Squeezecloud, Radio Stations grouped under a folder), the Favorites list will render emptier than expected.

## Trigger to promote to P2

- TestFlight tester complains about missing favorites OR
- A specific user identified with all-folder favorites

## Implementation sketch

Drill-down via `.fullScreenCover` (matches 98q.7 Visualizer + 9bb Queue patterns — see learning `tvos-nav-push-hides-tabbar`):

- Folder rows in FavoritesView render with a folder icon + chevron
- Tap pushes a child FavoritesView via .fullScreenCover
- Child view fetches `["favorites", "items"], ["item_id:N", "menu:favorites", "menu:1"]`
- Recursive (folder-of-folders supported)
- `.onExitCommand` on inner NavigationStack catches Menu to dismiss

Reference: lms-material `browse-resp.js:2414` uses `["menu:favorites", "menu:1"]` for hierarchical menu mode; flat mode uses `["want_url:1", "feedMode:1"]`.

## Out of scope

- Playlist favorites support (different code path — `playlist load` instead of `favorites playlist play`)
- Search-within-favorites
- Drag-to-reorder

## Depends on / blocks
- Depends on 98q.9 having shipped FavoritesView
- Does not block any other v1 work
acceptance_criteria: Folder favorites are navigable via Siri Remote drill-down. Recursive folders supported. Tab strip remains visible during drill-down (uses .fullScreenCover, not NavigationLink push).
close_reason: Device-verified in 2026-07-11 testing round: favorites folder drill works on Apple TV

CarPlay build 18 (4622a2f, k63) already implemented exactly this: recursive folder drill via favorites items 0 100 item_id:<id> want_url:1, parseLoop retains folders with isFolder, folder rows get a chevron, guarded stack depth. tvOS should follow the same wire pattern with the .fullScreenCover drill sketch in this bead (or reuse BrowseDestination — HomeExtraShelvesView already hosts a shared drill stack for albumTracks/playlistTracks/plugin, a .favoritesFolder case would slot in).

title: tvOS: Siri Remote hardware play/pause button does not toggle MPRemoteCommandCenter targets
description:
## Symptom
On tvOS, pressing the physical play/pause button on the Siri Remote (1st gen / circle-on-top remote) does NOT toggle playback on any tab. Tested on the 9bb build (TabView refactor) but the wiring is byte-identical to 98q.5, so this is a pre-existing issue surfaced by deliberate hardware testing for the first time.

## Diagnostic Confidence
HIGH — the user explicitly reports the hardware button doesn't fire MPRemoteCommandCenter targets. The togglePlayPauseCommand.addTarget closure at LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/ContentView.swift:160 captures the coordinator and routes through coordinator.sendLockScreenCommand(playing ? "pause" : "play"). If hit, audio would toggle. It is not being hit.

## What's Wired (98q.5)
- MPRemoteCommandCenter targets registered in ContentView.registerRemoteCommands() once connected, gated by remoteCommandsRegistered flag
- NowPlayingManager updates MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.nowPlayingInfo with title/artist/album/artwork/playback rate (no #if guards, applies on tvOS)
- center.togglePlayPauseCommand.isEnabled = true
- center.togglePlayPauseCommand.removeTarget(nil) + addTarget closure

## Hypotheses (need investigation)
1. MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.playbackState may need to be set explicitly on tvOS (iOS uses MPNowPlayingPlaybackState .playing/.paused). NowPlayingManager updates nowPlayingInfo[MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyPlaybackRate] but not playbackState.
2. AVAudioSession activation is iOS-only in this codebase (Group E share guards setActive() with #if os(iOS)). On tvOS, BASS may not need an audio session, but MPRemoteCommandCenter dispatch may require the app to be the system 'now playing' app, which on tvOS is gated by some other activation pattern.
3. Possible UIPress / responder chain consumption — the focused view (NowPlayingView playback panel or artwork tile) may be intercepting UIPress.PlayPause before MPRemoteCommandCenter sees it. Squeezelite-style remote-control on tvOS may need a UIResponder override on the SwiftUI hosting view.
4. Possible: tvOS 26 specific behavior change where MPRemoteCommandCenter on tvOS requires AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setActive(true) even though tvOS doesn't have iOS-style sessions (or the equivalent).

## Repro
1. Connect to LMS, start playback
2. Confirm Now Playing tab shows track + playback panel
3. Press the physical play/pause button on Siri Remote
4. Expected: audio pauses
5. Actual: nothing happens

## What ISN'T the cause
- Wiring is identical to 98q.5 → 9bb has no regression here. The wiki's 'Resolved' note for Open Question #4 in Architecture/tvOS Target.md was based on theoretical wiring, not hardware verification.
- nowPlayingInfo IS being set (verified in NowPlayingManager.swift:227-241 and 310-338, no #if guards).

## Next steps (separate session)
- Add os_log inside togglePlayPauseCommand.addTarget closure to confirm whether the closure ever fires when the button is pressed
- Compare against squeezelite tvOS / known-working tvOS audio apps for activation pattern
- Consult Apple sosumi docs for tvOS MPRemoteCommandCenter requirements
- Check if MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.playbackState (the dedicated enum, not nowPlayingInfo dict) needs to be set on tvOS

## Wiki update needed
Architecture/tvOS Target.md Open Question #4 should be un-struck from 'resolved' to 'needs hardware verification'. Will land in same commit that ships 9bb.

## Related
- 98q.5 (Now Playing): introduced the wiring (commit 2d01594). Wiki claim of resolution was unverified.
- LMS_StreamTest-9bb (TabView nav): not blocked by this; pre-existing issue surfaced during hardware testing.
close_reason: Hardware-verified fix shipped in commits c565627 + e9fc605 on tvos-target. Root cause: BASS_CONFIG_IOS_SESSION is iOS-only (BASS_CONFIG_IOS_SESSION.html:29), so on tvOS BASS does NOT auto-manage AVAudioSession; tvOS target had no UIBackgroundModes either. Fix: AudioManager.activateAudioSession() does real setCategory(.playback)+setActive(true) on tvOS (eager call after super.init); switched tvOS target from GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE to explicit Info.plist (Xcode 26 silently drops INFOPLIST_KEY_UIBackgroundModes from tvOS auto-generator); SwiftUI .onPlayPauseCommand fallbacks at ContentView TabView root + SearchView (.searchable intercepts UIPress) + QueueView (.fullScreenCover separate responder chain), all routing through new SlimProtoCoordinator.toggleLockScreenPlayPause() which uses synchronous commandHandler.isPausedByLockScreen flag (avoids 2x-press race from server STAT lag). HW play/pause + background audio verified on Apple TV 4K Siri Remote gen 1. tvOS HW play/pause is asymmetric: MPRC pauseCommand fires while playing, but MPRC playCommand does NOT fire when paused — SwiftUI .onPlayPauseCommand fallback is required for resume. Follow-up bd-g1d filed for tvOS audio interruption handling.

title: tvOS: scrub state can stick on vertical swipe, freezing progress bar / showing stale elapsed across track change
description:
## Symptom

On the tvOS Now Playing screen, two related symptoms (same root cause):
1. Progress bar / time label freezes mid-track. Track audio continues, but the displayed elapsed stops advancing.
2. After tapping a row in the Queue to jump tracks, the progress bar continues to show the previous track's elapsed time (often against the new track's shorter duration → bar overflows past the right edge) until the user does something else.

Reproduces on tvOS Simulator (LMS at 192.168.1.8). Build: 98q.6 (commit d7ee748).

## Root cause (corrected diagnosis)

NOT a SimpleTimeTracker / non-gapless-skip issue. iOS lock screen extrapolates elapsed via MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyPlaybackRate and is unaffected. The bug is local to LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/NowPlayingView.swift.

`handleMove` (NowPlayingView.swift:341-362) sets `isScrubbing = true` BEFORE validating the direction:

```swift
if !isScrubbing {
    isScrubbing = true              // set unconditionally
    scrubElapsed = elapsed
}

switch direction {
case .left:  scrubElapsed -= 10
case .right: scrubElapsed += 10
case .up, .down:
    return                          // exits before scheduleScrubCommit()
}

scheduleScrubCommit()              // only place that arms isScrubbing = false
```

`scheduleScrubCommit` is the only path that schedules `isScrubbing = false`. A spurious `.up`/`.down` from the Siri Remote touchpad (trivially easy — any vertical drift on a tap registers as vertical) flips `isScrubbing = true` and never releases it.

Once stuck:
- `tick()` (NowPlayingView.swift:332): `if !isScrubbing { elapsed = interpolated }` — `elapsed` stops updating.
- `progressRow` (NowPlayingView.swift:197): `displayElapsed = isScrubbing ? scrubElapsed : elapsed` — bar reads `scrubElapsed`, frozen at the moment of the spurious vertical swipe.
- Track change later: `metadataDuration` updates (different code path), but `scrubElapsed` does not → bar shows stale time against new duration.

This explains BOTH user-reported symptoms with the same bug.

Secondary: `scheduleScrubCommit` schedules an inner `asyncAfter(+0.6s) { isScrubbing = false }` that is NOT held in a cancellable work item. If a new swipe arrives during that release window, it silently clobbers an in-progress scrub.

## Fix (v1 must + polish trio)

Single-file change in LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/NowPlayingView.swift:

1. **Direction-filter-first in handleMove**: validate direction, only enter scrub state for .left/.right. Vertical events return without state mutation.
2. **Cancellable release**: store the deferred `isScrubbing = false` as a `releaseWorkItem` so it can be cancelled by subsequent swipes / cancel / commit-now.
3. **Visual scrub affordance**: when `isScrubbing`, bold the time label and tint with `accentColor` so the user sees they're in scrub mode.
4. **Click-to-commit** via `.onTapGesture` on the focused playback panel: touchpad click commits the scrub immediately (cancel pending workitems, seek now, release). Falls through to play/pause toggle when not scrubbing.
5. **Menu-to-cancel** via `.onExitCommand` on the playback panel: when scrubbing, snap `scrubElapsed = elapsed`, cancel both work items, release.

## Verify

- tvOS Simulator: focus playback panel, swipe up/down → progress bar must continue advancing (no freeze).
- tvOS Simulator: swipe left/right → time label flips bold + accent. Wait → debounce commits and label returns to secondary after STAT. Or click touchpad → commits immediately.
- tvOS Simulator: swipe left/right then press Menu → label snaps back to current elapsed, release. NavigationLink stays put (we are at root).
- tvOS Simulator: swipe several times rapidly, then tap a Queue row → progress bar shows new track's elapsed=0, not stale scrubElapsed.
- iOS regression: shared file is tvOS-target-only, no iOS impact possible.

## Affected files
- LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/NowPlayingView.swift (entire scrub state machine + visual affordance)
close_reason: Shipped in 277fb83. Click-to-enter scrubber model with thumb, explicit commit/cancel, .onMoveCommand only attached while scrubbing. Plus tech info line and font/contrast polish.

title: tvOS: root navigation (TabView between Visualizer and Search)
description:
Introduce a root-level navigation container so v1 peer screens (Now Playing, Search, Favorites/Recents) can coexist. Must land between 98q.7 (Visualizer) and 98q.8 (Search) — Visualizer is an in-place Now Playing treatment and doesn't need new nav, but Search is a peer destination that can't be pushed onto Now Playing's NavigationStack.

Current shape (post-98q.6):
  NavigationStack
  └── NowPlayingView (root)
      └── QueueView (push)

Target shape (after this ticket):
  TabView at ContentView root
  ├── Now Playing tab → NowPlayingView → Queue (push), Visualizer (overlay/toggle)
  ├── Search tab → SearchView (98q.8)
  └── Library tab → Favorites / Recents (98q.9)

Implementation notes:
- TabView on tvOS renders as a focusable top tab bar — the platform-native pattern (matches Apple Music tvOS, TV app, App Store). Sidebar is the alternative (Plex pattern); start with TabView.
- D2 invariant from 98q.5: MPRemoteCommandCenter targets must remain registered at ContentView level, not inside any individual tab. Tab switching MUST NOT tear down Siri Remote responsiveness. Verify before/after each tab switch that hardware play/pause still works.
- Focus engine: tvOS TabView default focus moves to the active tab's content on appear. Test that swipe-up from playback focuses the tab bar, swipe-down returns to content. Default tab on launch = Now Playing.
- NavigationStack-per-tab: each tab has its own NavigationStack so sub-pushes (Queue from Now Playing, search-result detail from Search) don't cross tabs.
- The 4th transport button → QueueView push from 98q.6 should keep working unchanged inside the Now Playing tab's stack.
- Empty state: if no track loaded, Now Playing tab shows the existing empty state. Search tab works regardless. Favorites tab works regardless.

Open questions to resolve in plan-eng-review for this ticket:
- TabView vs sidebar — taste call, but TabView is more tvOS-native.
- Where does Visualizer (98q.7) live? Likely a full-screen overlay/toggle from Now Playing tab content, NOT its own tab.
- Tab order: [Now Playing | Search | Library]? Or library-first like Apple Music? Defer to plan-eng-review.
- Migration: ContentView currently holds MPRemoteCommandCenter target wiring + connection state polling. Refactor so TabView is the body and MPRemoteCommandCenter wiring stays at the same scope (above TabView).

Out of scope:
- Library tree (Artists/Albums/Genres/Apps) — explicitly v2 per design doc.
- Settings tab — v1 doesn't have one yet; if added, it's a separate ticket.

Acceptance:
- All four v1 destinations (Now Playing + Queue, Visualizer-as-overlay, Search, Favorites/Recents) are reachable via the tab bar without push depth > 2.
- D2 invariant verified manually on Apple TV.
- iOS app unaffected (tvOS-only changes).

Sequencing: ships AFTER 98q.7 (Visualizer prototype + production view). Ships BEFORE 98q.8 (Search). 98q.9 (Favorites + Recents) builds on this.
close_reason: Closed

title: tvOS: Search via Siri Remote dictation
description: Siri Remote voice search. Use UISearchController wrapped in UISearchContainerViewController via UIViewControllerRepresentable. SwiftUI .searchable alone does NOT give dictation on tvOS. Wire results to JSON-RPC 'search' query.
acceptance_criteria: User presses Siri Remote search button, dictates query, sees results from LMS within 2 seconds. Results are focusable rows that jump to track or load album.
notes:
## Reuse map (98q.9 infrastructure to leverage)

Search rendering is a near-perfect fit for the Library tab’s shape:

- `MediaRow<Trailing:>` for every result row. Tracks → trailing duration label; Albums → trailing year (or empty); Artists → empty; Playlists → empty.
- `LMSArtworkURL.cover(coverID:fallbackID:settings:)` for track + album + playlist artwork. Artist results have no artwork in the standard `artists tags:s` shape — placeholder.
- `Album.parseLoop`, `Playlist.parseLoop`, `PlaylistTrack.parseLoop` all already exist (PlaylistModels.swift). Add a small `Artist.parseLoop` to round out per-domain parsing.
- Tap-to-play parallels Library exactly:
  - Track → `["playlistcontrol","cmd:load","track_id:N"]` (player-targeted)
  - Album → `["playlistcontrol","cmd:load","album_id:N"]` (matches AlbumListView:166)
  - Playlist → `["playlistcontrol","cmd:load","playlist_id:N"]` (matches PlaylistsView:117)
  - Artist → drill into albums-by-artist, OR play-all? See open question 3.

## JSON-RPC strategy (verified against slimserver + lms-material)

**lms-material does NOT use the unified `["search", ...]` query.** Per `search-field.js:182-192`, Material fires SEPARATE per-domain queries each carrying `search:<term>`:

- `["artists", 0, N, "tags:s", "search:<term>"]`
- `["albums", 0, N, "tags:laetc", "search:<term>"]`
- `["tracks", 0, N, "tags:elcy", "search:<term>"]`
- `["playlists", 0, N, "tags:su", "search:<term>"]`
- `["globalsearch","items","menu:1","search:<term>"]` — online sources (Spotify/Tidal/etc.)

This is a load-bearing detail: the per-domain returns ARE the same `<type>s_loop` shapes that 98q.9’s parsers already consume, with no second parse path. Lock to per-domain queries; defer `globalsearch` (online sources) past v1 unless trivial.

For comparison, slimserver has a unified `["search", index, quantity, "term:<query>"]` (`Slim/Control/Queries.pm:3474-3661`) returning `contributors_loop`, `albums_loop`, `works_loop`, `genres_loop`, `tracks_loop` — but no playlist results (per `# XXX - should we search for playlists, too?` comment) and slightly different field names (`contributor_id` vs `id`). Not used here.

## Open questions for plan-eng-review

1. **UISearchController vs SwiftUI .searchable in tvOS 26.** Design doc / current bd description says `.searchable` alone does NOT give Siri Remote dictation on tvOS. tvOS 26 may have changed this. Verify against current SDK first; if `.searchable` works, skip the UIViewControllerRepresentable wrapper and the focus-engine handoff complexity. If still required, plan the focus boundary handoff (UIKit text field ↔ SwiftUI focus engine) explicitly — the on-screen keyboard “Done” return path is the failure point.

2. **Search scope architecture: cross-domain vs per-scope tabs vs unified flat list.**
   - **Sectioned single screen** (Material UI shape): one query string, fire 4 parallel per-domain queries, render results as List sections — Artists / Albums / Tracks / Playlists. Material precedent. Best UX for “I don’t know what type I’m looking for”.
   - **Per-scope sub-tabs** (Picker like Library): tap Tracks / Albums / Artists / Playlists segment, query just that one. Cheaper queries, but extra hop per intent.
   - **Recommend sectioned single screen.** Matches Material, matches the Library tab’s “present what’s there” energy, makes one fewer focus-engine surface.

3. **Artist tap behavior.** Material drills into artist’s albums (`albums search-by-contributor`). v1 simpler:
   - Option A: drill into artist → AlbumListView-style albums-by-artist (new lightweight artist-detail view).
   - Option B: play-all-by-artist via `["playlistcontrol","cmd:load","artist_id:N"]` on tap.
   - Option C: hide artist results entirely for v1 (tracks + albums + playlists only). Cuts scope; matches “Search what’s playable now” framing.
   - Recommend B for v1 (matches “tap-to-play, stay on Library” D6 pattern from 98q.9). Option A is a v2 ticket if users ask.

4. **Debounce timeout.** lms-material uses **500ms** (`search-field.js:168`, `search-list.js:124`). User-briefing said 300ms. Pick one, with reasoning. Recommend matching Material’s 500ms — Siri Remote dictation arrives in chunks (not per-keystroke), so 500ms gives the dictation engine time to consolidate without “almost there” partial-word queries hammering the server. Cancel any in-flight request when the term changes (Material uses an incrementing `seachReqId` to drop stale responses — mirror this).

5. **Result limits per domain.** Material clamps to `LMS_INITIAL_SEARCH_RESULTS` (≈25) with a “show all” expansion. v1 simpler: cap each domain at 25 (or 50?) and don’t bother with “show all” — the 95th percentile query will fit inside that. Specify in plan-eng-review.

6. **Empty / no-results / pre-search states.**
   - Pre-search (no query yet): blank, OR “Recently played searches” (Material has history). v1 simpler: blank with a centered hint (“Press the Siri Remote search button and dictate”).
   - In-flight: ProgressView (matches Library sub-views).
   - No results (query returned 0): friendly “No results for ‘<query>’” centered card.

7. **Where is the search-field UI?** Two options:
   - At the TOP of the Search tab content (Material shape). Default focus moves to the field on tab activation.
   - Modal-presented via Siri Remote search button only, dismissed back to a results view. tvOS canonical pattern — but means the tab needs a useful “resting state” to show when the modal isn’t up. Probably option A is simpler for v1.

## Constraints to honor

- **D2 invariant (98q.5):** MPRemoteCommandCenter target wiring stays in `ContentView` ABOVE the TabView. Search tab MUST NOT register or remove MP targets in its onAppear/onDisappear.
- **Group E share (98q.4a):** Work is tvOS-only (`LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/`). The only shared-side change permitted is adding `Artist` model + `Artist.parseLoop` to `PlaylistModels.swift` (Group A — share unchanged) if needed.
- **`tvos-tabview-onappear-focus-restore` (9/10):** Any deferred-focus / `.onAppear`-driven focus state setter MUST be gated by a `didInitialFocus: Bool` flag. Each tab re-selection triggers `.onAppear`, which would otherwise stomp tab-restored focus.
- **No SearchPlaceholderView leftovers:** delete the placeholder struct from ContentView.swift when wiring SearchView in; don’t leave dead-code stubs.
- **Adversarial review hardening from 98q.6/98q.9:**
  - `ForEach` identity: prefer `.id` (parsed item id) over `.offset`. The 98q.9 /review pass switched Albums + Playlists to `.id` for stable diffing on incremental updates. Search results re-render on every keystroke-after-debounce; `.offset` would force the entire list to re-mount and lose focus.
  - In-flight request cancellation: Material uses an incrementing request id and drops stale responses. Mirror with a `currentQueryToken: UUID` + token-check in the completion handler.

## Scope clarification

**In v1:**
- Sectioned single screen with Tracks + Albums + Playlists (and Artists if Q3 = B or A).

**Out of v1:**

- Search history (Material’s 20-item recency list). Defer.
- Advanced search (Material’s separate dialog with library_id/genre/year filters). Defer.

title: tvOS: Library tab — Favorites + RP + New Music + Playlists
description:
Two list-view screens replacing the LibraryPlaceholderView stub from 98q-9bb (`LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/ContentView.swift:219-233`):

- **Favorites** — vanilla LMS `["favorites", "items"]` JSON-RPC (verified via lms-material `server.js:873` and `browse-resp.js:2414`)
- **Recently Played** — vanilla LMS `["albums"], ["sort:recentlyplayed", ALBUM_TAGS_ALL_ARTISTS]` (verified via lms-material `browse-resp.js:2403` — Material's home-menu "Recently Played" entry uses this exact pattern). Track-granularity history would require the `playhistory` plugin which is NOT vanilla; albums-granularity is the v1 path.

Same focus-engine list pattern as Queue (98q.6, `QueueView.swift`) — reuse the row component once it's built.

## Open questions to resolve in plan-eng-review

### Q1 — Sub-tab structure within the Library tab
Library tab needs to host TWO peer destinations. Three patterns:
  - **(a) Sub-tabs / segmented control at top of content** — Apple Music TV pattern (secondary tab strip below the primary TabView). Most native to "this is a library with two views". On tvOS, `Picker(.segmented)` is focusable.
  - **(b) NavigationLink list** — Library root shows two big rows ("Favorites" / "Recently Played"), each pushes to a list view. **Triggers `tvos-nav-push-hides-tabbar` (9/10 learning)** — the primary tab strip would auto-hide on push and not reliably restore. Would need `.fullScreenCover` (Visualizer/Queue pattern from 98q.7/9bb), which feels heavy for two simple drill-downs.
  - **(c) Single combined list with section headers** — one screen, two `Section`s. Simplest, but conflates two distinct things and breaks the parity with the design doc's "Favorites + Recently Played" framing.

My read: (a) is the right call — native, no nav quirks, matches Apple Music TV.

### Q2 — Row component reuse from QueueView
`QueueRow` is `private struct` inside `QueueView.swift` (lines 203-300). For 98q.9 (and 98q.8 search results later), should we extract it to a reusable `MediaRow` component, or copy-and-modify because the affordances differ? Per learning `audit-overcounts-iOS-coupling`, default to share/extract over fork unless divergence is large.

Affordance comparison:
  - QueueRow: artwork + title + artist + (current-track speaker indicator | duration)
  - Favorites row: artwork + title + (favorite-type badge — radio icon, podcast, track, etc.) + maybe URL/source line
  - Recently Played row: artwork + album title + artist + (year? play-count? timestamp?) — and it's an album, not a track

Variation level: trailing accessory + secondary line differ; left side (artwork + primary text) is identical. Suggests an extracted base row with a trailing closure / view slot for the accessory.

### Q3 — Favorites: flat vs hierarchical
LMS Favorites can be folders (e.g., "Radio Stations / BBC Radio 3"). Material supports drill-down (`browse-resp.js:2414` uses `["menu:favorites", "menu:1"]` for hierarchical menu mode).

For v1, two choices:
  - **Top-level flat (skip folders)** — call `["favorites", "items"], ["want_url:1", "feedMode:1"]` and render only items with playable URLs. Simpler. Risk: users with all-folder favorites see empty list.
  - **Drill-down folders** — render folder rows that push to a child view. Brings back the `tvos-nav-push-hides-tabbar` concern from Q1 — even with sub-tabs (Q1a), folder navigation is push-within-Library. Acceptable if drilling into a folder hides the secondary tab strip but not the primary TabView strip; needs verification.

Suggest v1 = flat-with-folder-support: render folder rows but flat-list mode for the common case; defer hierarchical browse to v2 if needed. Or just flat-flat for v1 and add folders as `LMS_StreamTest-NEW` follow-up.

### Q4 — Tap-to-play behavior
Three options:
  - **(i) Replace queue + start playing** — CarPlay's pattern (`CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift` browse → `playlist play` ID). Simplest for v1.
  - **(ii) Add to end of queue** — `playlist add` ID. User-friendly but requires a "play now" affordance.
  - **(iii) Jump-in-current-queue** — only works if track already in playlist; not generally applicable here.

For Favorites: the canonical action is `["favorites", "playlist", "play"]` per `constants.js:279` (RADIOS_BASE_ACTIONS). For Recently Played albums: `["playlistcontrol"], ["cmd:load", "album_id:N"]`. v1 = (i) for both.

### Q5 — On-demand fetch pattern
Per learning `tvos-queue-data-source-ondemand`, prefer `coordinator.sendJSONRPCCommandDirect` on `.onAppear` (and on track change for Queue) over a long-lived `ObservableObject`. Same shape as `QueueView.fetchPlaylist()`.

For Favorites: `.onAppear` only — favorites list rarely changes mid-session.
For Recently Played: `.onAppear` AND `.onChange(of: nowPlaying.currentTrackTitle)` — when a new track plays the recently-played list updates server-side.

### Q6 — Empty / loading / error states
Both screens need:
  - Loading: `ProgressView` overlay (Queue uses an `isLoading` flag without visible progress; for first-load on a slow LAN we should show one).
  - Empty: friendly empty state. Recently Played on a fresh server will be empty until something is played.
  - Error: silent-fail (keep prior list) like Queue, OR explicit retry button? v1 = silent-fail + log; the list re-fetches on next `.onAppear`.

### Q7 — Pagination
Favorites: usually small (<50 items), no paging needed in v1. Cap at 100.
Recently Played albums: server typically returns ~25-50 by default. Cap at 100. Per learning `tvos-queue-data-source-ondemand`, no virtualization needed at this scale.

### Q8 — Constraints (do NOT regress)
- D2 invariant from 98q.5 / 98q-9bb: MPRemoteCommandCenter wiring stays in `ContentView.registerRemoteCommands` ABOVE the TabView. Library tab adds NO new media control concerns.
- Group E share: 98q.9 work is pure tvOS UI — **only `LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/` files**. JSON-RPC goes through shared `SlimProtoCoordinator` (already shared via Group E). If `MediaRow` is extracted, it stays in `LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/` — tvOS-only UI.
- `tvos-tabview-onappear-focus-restore` (9/10): if any view inside the Library tab uses deferred-focus pattern (`DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter { focused = true }`), gate it with a `@State didInitialFocus` flag.
- `tvos-nav-push-hides-tabbar` (9/10): drives Q1 and Q3.

## Out of scope
- Library tree (Artists/Albums/Genres/Apps/Playlists) — explicitly v2 per design doc.
- Hierarchical Favorites browse (folders) — defer to v2 or follow-up if Q3 lands flat.
- Recently Played at track-granularity (requires `playhistory` plugin).
- Top Shelf integration — v2.

## Acceptance
- Library tab opens to a sub-tab/segmented view exposing Favorites + Recently Played (per Q1 resolution).
- Favorites tab shows LMS favorites items list, navigable with Siri Remote, click loads/plays via `["favorites", "playlist", "play"]`.
- Recently Played tab shows recently-played albums, navigable, click loads via `["playlistcontrol"], ["cmd:load", "album_id:N"]`.
- Tab strip stays visible across all interactions (verified on Apple TV hardware per 9bb manual-verification protocol).
- D2 invariant preserved: hardware play/pause behavior unchanged from 9bb baseline (still tracked by `LMS_StreamTest-bia`).
- iOS app unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: Favorites shows LMS favorites list. Recently Played shows recently played tracks. Both navigable with Siri Remote, click loads/plays.

title: CarPlay forward/back buttons grayed out after CarPlay resume from cold start
description:
## Symptom
Sometimes when starting LyrPlay in the car, playback resumes via CarPlay recovery, but the next/previous track buttons on the CarPlay Now Playing screen appear grayed out / disabled.

## Mechanism
CarPlay's prev/next track buttons are driven by `MPRemoteCommandCenter.shared().{previousTrackCommand,nextTrackCommand}.isEnabled`. The only place that disables them at runtime is `NowPlayingManager.updatePlaylistPosition(currentIndex:totalTracks:)`:

```swift
commandCenter.previousTrackCommand.isEnabled = (currentIndex > 0)
commandCenter.nextTrackCommand.isEnabled = (currentIndex < totalTracks - 1)
```

For BOTH to be disabled simultaneously, we need `currentIndex == 0 AND totalTracks <= 1`.

## Hypotheses
1. **Server transient state**: After the playlist-jump recovery (`performPlaylistRecovery → playlist jump`), `fetchCurrentTrackMetadata()` fires 1s later. If LMS hasn't fully processed the jump yet, it may briefly report `playlist_tracks=1` for the queued track being recovered. The metadata fetch happens once and never retries — so buttons stay wrong.

2. **Stale single-track context**: User was previously playing a single-track radio stream → totalTracks correctly = 1. On recovery, this state persists. (Behavior may be technically correct but confusing to user.)

3. **JSON-RPC type coercion**: `result["playlist_tracks"] as? Int` returns nil if server sends value as string in some response paths → block does not run, but neither does the update — so buttons stay in their previous (enabled) state. Doesn't match symptom.

## Verification Path
1. Add log to `parseTrackMetadata` (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1892) printing the raw `result["playlist_tracks"]` and `result["playlist_cur_index"]` values + types
2. Add log to `updatePlaylistPosition` printing what was passed
3. Reproduce by killing app, ensuring CarPlay is connected, opening app from CarPlay
4. Compare what server returned vs the playlist user expected to see

## Possible Fix
- Re-fetch metadata 5-10s after recovery to catch up to server state
- Or: only call `updatePlaylistPosition` if `playlist_loop.count > 1` matches `totalTracks` (sanity check)
- Or: separate next/prev button enabling from playlist position — keep them enabled by default and only disable on actual server "no next" response

## Files
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1884-1899 (parseTrackMetadata)
- LMS_StreamTest/NowPlayingManager.swift:425-439 (updatePlaylistPosition)
- LMS_StreamTest/CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:150-202 (resume path)
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:443-533 (executePlaylistRecovery)

## Related
- LMS_StreamTest-u7h: Likely independent bug in same area (post-call no-audio)

title: Add LMS Favorites browse to CarPlay menu
description:
# Add LMS Favorites browse to CarPlay menu

User-requested feature from forums: surface LMS Favorites in the CarPlay browse UI so users can play favorited tracks, albums, radio stations, podcasts, and plugin content (Spotify/TIDAL/etc.) without touching the phone.

## Recommended Approach

**Flat home + tree Favorites with depth cap (pop-to-root fallback if we'd exceed CarPlay's 5-template stack).**

### Why this approach

CarPlay caps the navigation stack at 5 templates (see comment at `CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:214`). Our current Artists browse already uses all 5: Home → A–Z range → Artists → Albums → Tracks. Adding a "Browse" submenu wrapper would push that to 6 and break it. Tree Favorites with deeply nested user folders (Classical → Chamber → Album → Tracks under Favorites) can also hit the limit.

Solution: keep the home menu flat, insert Favorites as a sibling, and cap Favorites drill-down depth — if we'd push a 4th level inside Favorites, pop-to-root before pushing the next template (or play the item directly if it's audio).

### Proposed Home Menu Structure

```
LyrPlay
├── ▶︎ Resume Playback
├── New Music (image row)
├── Random Releases (image row)
├── Favorites            ← NEW (top-tier, above Playlists)
├── Playlists
├── Artists (A–Z)
├── Random Artists
├── More Random Releases
└── Refresh
```

Rationale: Favorites and Playlists are user-curated and used most often in the car; random/discovery items are exploration tools that belong lower. Flat beats nested when eyes-on-road time matters.

### Why NOT a "Browse" submenu

Bundling Artists/Random Artists/Random Albums/Playlists/Favorites under one "Browse" entry would be cleaner but adds a level to every drill-down. Already at-limit Artists path would break (6 levels). Off the table unless we collapse the A–Z range step too.

## Favorites Content Types

Favorites is heterogeneous, not just songs. Each item has `isaudio` and `hasitems` flags:

| Type | `isaudio` | `hasitems` | Example |
|------|-----------|------------|---------|
| Track | 1 | 0 | Individual song |
| Album/playlist | 0 | 1 | Expands to tracks |
| Radio station | 1 | 0 | Internet radio URL |
| Podcast | 0 | 1 | Episode list |
| User folder | 0 | 1 | Your own grouping |
| Plugin root | 0 | 1 | Spotify/TIDAL/Qobuz/BBC browse |
| App link | varies | varies | Service-specific |

Flattening to `isaudio:1` only would lose folders, podcasts, and plugin browses (a big chunk of what power users put in Favorites). Tree navigation with depth cap is the right tradeoff.

## JSON-RPC API

LMS exposes a tree-structured `favorites items` endpoint that mirrors what Material shows:

**List root favorites:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "method": "slim.request",
  "params": ["", ["favorites", "items", 0, 100, "want_url:1"]]
}
```

**Drill into folder:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "method": "slim.request",
  "params": ["", ["favorites", "items", 0, 100, "item_id:<id>", "want_url:1"]]
}
```

**Play a favorite (use player MAC):**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "method": "slim.request",
  "params": ["<player-mac>", ["favorites", "playlist", "play", "item_id:<id>"]]
}
```

Verify the exact response shape against `http://<server>:9000/?material=debug` before implementing — the response has a `loop_loop` array with each item containing `id`, `name`, `icon`, `isaudio`, `hasitems`, `url`.

## Implementation Notes

- Pattern mirrors existing `fetchPlaylists` → `displayPlaylists` → `handlePlaylistSelection` flow at `CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:710`
- Reuse `coordinator.sendJSONRPCCommandDirect` for all favorites queries
- Reuse `loadArtwork` at `CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:826` — favorites items have `icon` URLs that may be either LMS coverIDs or external URLs; handle both
- Add `cachedFavorites: [FavoriteItem]` to the cached data block at `CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:11-14` if we want eager loading on connect; otherwise lazy-fetch on tap
- Update `buildHomeTemplateSections()` at `CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:1147` to insert the new Favorites row

title: CarPlay Siri search integration - voice commands like 'play Taylor Swift'
description:
## Feature Request

Enable Siri voice commands in CarPlay and iOS like "Hey Siri, play Taylor Swift in LyrPlay"

## Implementation Approach: Hybrid (Search in Extension, Play in App)

### Why This Approach
- **Extension resolves media** → Siri confirms "Playing Taylor Swift" (better voice feedback)
- **Extension returns `.handleInApp`** → Main app handles actual playback via existing infrastructure
- **App Group for settings** → Share host/port/credentials/playerMAC with extension
- **Duplicate JSON-RPC helper** → Only ~40 lines, avoids shared framework complexity

### Architecture Flow

```
User: "Hey Siri, play Taylor Swift in LyrPlay"
         ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Intents Extension Process           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. resolveMediaItems() called               │
│ 2. Read server settings from App Group      │
│ 3. JSON-RPC search: ["artists", "search:X"] │
│ 4. Return INMediaItem with artist_id        │
│ 5. Siri says "Playing Taylor Swift"         │
│ 6. handle() returns .handleInApp            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Main App Process                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. AppDelegate receives INPlayMediaIntent   │
│ 2. Extract identifier (e.g. "artist_id:123")│
│ 3. playlistcontrol cmd:load artist_id:123   │
│ 4. Existing SlimProto handles playback      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Settings to Share via App Group

```swift
// Write to App Group UserDefaults in SettingsManager
let sharedDefaults = UserDefaults(suiteName: "group.elm.LyrPlay")
sharedDefaults?.set(activeServerHost, forKey: "serverHost")
sharedDefaults?.set(activeServerWebPort, forKey: "serverWebPort") 
sharedDefaults?.set(activeServerUsername, forKey: "serverUsername")
sharedDefaults?.set(activeServerPassword, forKey: "serverPassword")
sharedDefaults?.set(playerMACAddress, forKey: "playerMAC")
```

### LMS Search Commands (for Extension)

**Search Artists:**
```json
["artists", "0", "10", "tags:s", "search:Taylor Swift"]
```

**Search Albums:**
```json
["albums", "0", "10", "tags:ljy", "search:1989"]
```

**Search Tracks:**
```json
["tracks", "0", "10", "tags:dlt", "search:Shake It Off"]
```

### Playback Command (for Main App)

```swift
// In AppDelegate, reuse existing SlimProtoCoordinator
let command: [String: Any] = [
    "id": 1,
    "method": "slim.request",
    "params": [playerMAC, ["playlistcontrol", "cmd:load", identifier]]
]
coordinator.sendJSONRPCCommandDirect(command) { _ in }
```

### Key Code to Add

**IntentHandler.swift (Extension):**
```swift
class IntentHandler: INExtension, INPlayMediaIntentHandling {
    
    func resolveMediaItems(for intent: INPlayMediaIntent,
                           with completion: @escaping ([INPlayMediaItemResolutionResult]) -> Void) {
        guard let searchTerm = intent.mediaSearch?.mediaName else {
            completion([.unsupported()])
            return
        }
        
        searchLMS(query: searchTerm) { result in
            if let item = result {
                let mediaItem = INMediaItem(
                    identifier: item.id,  // "artist_id:123"
                    title: item.title,
                    type: .music,
                    artwork: nil
                )
                completion([.success(with: mediaItem)])
            } else {
                completion([.unsupported()])
            }
        }
    }
    
    func handle(intent: INPlayMediaIntent,
                completion: @escaping (INPlayMediaIntentResponse) -> Void) {
        // Let main app handle playback
        completion(INPlayMediaIntentResponse(code: .handleInApp, userActivity: nil))
    }
}
```

**AppDelegate.swift (Addition):**
```swift
func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                 handle intent: INIntent,
                 completionHandler: @escaping (INIntentResponse) -> Void) {
    
    if let playIntent = intent as? INPlayMediaIntent,
       let mediaItem = playIntent.mediaItems?.first,
       let identifier = mediaItem.identifier {
        // identifier is "artist_id:123", "album_id:456", or "track_id:789"
        playMediaFromSiri(identifier: identifier)
        completionHandler(INPlayMediaIntentResponse(code: .success, userActivity: nil))
    } else {
        completionHandler(INPlayMediaIntentResponse(code: .failure, userActivity: nil))
    }
}

private func playMediaFromSiri(identifier: String) {
    guard let coordinator = // get coordinator reference
    else { return }
    
    let playerMAC = SettingsManager.shared.playerMACAddress
    let command: [String: Any] = [
        "id": 1,
        "method": "slim.request", 
        "params": [playerMAC, ["playlistcontrol", "cmd:load", identifier]]
    ]
    coordinator.sendJSONRPCCommandDirect(command) { _ in }
}
```

## Existing Code to Reuse

- **`sendJSONRPCCommandDirect()`** - SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1603 (pattern to duplicate in extension)
- **`playlistcontrol` commands** - CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift (already implemented)
- **`generateAuthHeader()`** - SettingsManager.swift:622 (static method, can duplicate)

## References

- [WWDC19: Introducing SiriKit Media Intents](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2019/207/)
- [App Groups Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/configuring-app-groups)
- Material Skin: search-field.js, browse-functions.js

## Priority

P2 - Nice to have for hands-free CarPlay/iOS experience
notes:
## Existing Code to Reuse

The codebase already has JSON-RPC infrastructure that should be reused:

### Core Infrastructure (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift)
- **`sendJSONRPCCommandDirect()`** (line 1603) - Public method with:
  - Auth header support (HTTP Basic)
  - Custom User-Agent
  - Completion handler with response parsing
  - Already used by CarPlay

### Existing Query Commands (CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift)
- **Album query**: `["albums", 0, 8, "sort:new", "tags:ajlqy"]` (line 1303)
- **Track query by album**: `["titles", 0, 100, "album_id:X", "tags:daltC"]` (line 1494)  
- **Playlist tracks**: `["playlists", "tracks", 0, 1000, "playlist_id:X", "tags:dalC"]` (line 686)

### Existing Playback Commands (CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift)
- **Play album**: `["playlistcontrol", "cmd:load", "album_id:X"]` (line 1693)
- **Play album at track**: `["playlistcontrol", "cmd:load", "album_id:X", "play_index:Y"]` (line 1663)
- **Play playlist**: `["playlistcontrol", "cmd:load", "playlist_id:X", "play_index:0"]` (line 267)

### New Commands Needed for Siri Search
Only these search queries need to be added:
- `["artists", 0, 50, "tags:s", "search:X"]` - Artist search
- `["tracks", 0, 50, "tags:dlelyc", "search:X"]` - Track search  
- `["globalsearch", "items", 0, 50, "menu:1", "search:X"]` - Global search (optional)

### Implementation Approach
1. **Shared Framework**: Extract `sendJSONRPCCommandDirect()` into a shared framework/module that both main app and Intents Extension can use
2. **App Group**: Share server credentials via App Group container
3. **Reuse patterns**: Follow same JSON-RPC structure as CarPlaySceneDelegate

### Key Insight
The `playlistcontrol` command with `artist_id:`, `album_id:`, `track_id:` params already exists - just needs search queries to find those IDs.

title: MP3 transcode defaults to 128kbps - investigate server bitrate configuration
description:
## Issue

MP3 transcoding always defaults to 128kbps regardless of source quality. This results in unnecessary quality loss for mobile/transcode scenarios.

## Expected Behavior

- High-quality sources (FLAC, WAV) should transcode to higher bitrate MP3 (320kbps or at least 256kbps)
- Lower quality sources can use 128kbps or appropriate bitrate
- User should have control over transcode quality preference

## Current Behavior

All MP3 transcodes use 128kbps, even when transcoding lossless FLAC files.

## Investigation Areas

### 1. Server-Side Configuration

Check LMS server's `custom-convert.conf` file for MP3 transcode rules:
- Default bitrate settings
- Quality flags for lame/ffmpeg encoder
- Mobile-specific transcode rules

### 2. MobileTranscode Settings

The app uses `mobiletranscode` preference. Possible issues:
- Server default bitrate for mobile transcoding
- Missing quality parameter in transcode requests
- LMS plugin configuration for mobile devices

### 3. SlimProto Protocol

Review protocol messages:
- Does SlimProto support requesting specific bitrate?
- Are we sending quality preferences to server?
- Check STRM command parameters

## Likely Solution

Update `custom-convert.conf` on LMS server with higher quality MP3 settings for mobile transcode:

```bash
# Find current MP3 transcode rules
grep -A 5 "mp3" /path/to/custom-convert.conf

# Typical location: /etc/squeezeboxserver/custom-convert.conf
# Or: ~/Library/Application Support/Squeezebox/custom-convert.conf (macOS)
```

title: Test bit-perfect playback with USB DAC
description:
Test with FIIO KA17 or similar USB DAC: 96kHz FLAC (expect 96kHz on DAC), 192kHz FLAC (expect 192kHz), 44.1kHz MP3 (expect 44.1kHz). Verify DAC display shows native rates.

## Critical Fix Applied (Build 11 - December 2025)

### Bug Report from Tester
When playing playlists with mixed sample rates (e.g., 96kHz → 88.2kHz → 44.1kHz):
- Sample rate switched to NEXT track's rate during prefetching
- Brief silence when DAC switched rates mid-track  
- Current track got resampled to next track's rate (quality loss)
- **Example**: Track 1 at 96kHz resampled to 88.2kHz when Track 2 started buffering

### Root Cause
`AudioStreamDecoder.startDecodingFromURL()` (line 650) called `setPreferredSampleRate()` immediately when decoder stream was created during **PREFETCHING**, not when track actually started playing.

**Broken flow:**
```
1. Track 1 (96kHz) playing
2. LMS prefetches Track 2 (88.2kHz) → STRM command arrives
3. startDecodingFromURL() → decoder created for Track 2
4. setPreferredSampleRate(88200) called IMMEDIATELY ❌
5. iOS audio session switches 96kHz → 88.2kHz (Track 1 still playing!)
6. Track 1 gets resampled, brief silence on DAC
```

### Solution (Build 11)
Moved `setPreferredSampleRate()` from prefetch time (line 637-677) to stream creation time in `initializePushStream()` (line 354-395).

**Fixed flow:**
```
1. Track 1 (96kHz) playing
2. LMS prefetches Track 2 (88.2kHz) → decoder created
3. Format mismatch detected → stored as pendingTrack
4. Track 1 continues playing at 96kHz (undisturbed) ✅
5. Track 1 finishes → handleBufferEnd() → startDeferredTrack()
6. setPreferredSampleRate(88200) called NOW ✅
7. Push stream recreated with new format
8. Track 2 starts at 88.2kHz (clean transition)
```

### Files Changed (Commit 2d8c068)
- **AudioStreamDecoder.swift line 637-639**: Removed premature setPreferredSampleRate() call
- **AudioStreamDecoder.swift line 354-395**: Added to initializePushStream()

Now `setPreferredSampleRate()` only called when push stream actually created:
1. First track (AudioManager.swift:125)
2. Format mismatch, non-gapless (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:724)  
3. Format mismatch, gapless deferred (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1429 in startDeferredTrack)

### Testing Requirements
✅ Playlist with mixed rates: 96→88.2→44.1→96→48 kHz
✅ Sample rate changes at track boundary, not during buffering
✅ No premature resampling of current track
✅ No brief silence during playback
✅ Same sample rate tracks: No unnecessary rate changes
✅ External DAC display shows correct rate throughout each track

### Technical Details
The fix leverages existing `pendingTrack` deferred start mechanism for gapless format mismatches. When track formats differ:
1. New track decoder created but NOT started
2. Stored as `pendingTrack` with sample rate info
3. Current track plays to completion at original rate
4. Buffer empties → `handleBufferEnd()` triggered
5. iOS session rate changed → push stream recreated → deferred track started
6. Clean transition at track boundary

This ensures bit-perfect playback throughout each track with seamless transitions between different sample rates.

title: Test gapless transitions with sample rate changes
description:
Test gapless playback: 96kHz → 192kHz, 44.1kHz → 96kHz. Verify device reinits correctly during track boundaries without audio dropout.

## FIXED in Build 11 (December 2025)

### Previous Bug
Sample rate changes occurred during **prefetching** instead of at **track boundaries**, causing:
- Current track resampled mid-playback when next track buffered
- Brief silence on DAC during sample rate switch
- Quality loss from premature resampling

### Fix Applied
Moved `setPreferredSampleRate()` from `startDecodingFromURL()` (prefetch) to `initializePushStream()` (stream creation).

**Commit**: 2d8c068  
**Files**: AudioStreamDecoder.swift (lines 354-395, 637-639)

### How Gapless Sample Rate Changes Work Now

**Scenario: Track 1 (96kHz) → Track 2 (88.2kHz)**

1. **Track 1 playing at 96kHz**
   - Push stream created at 96kHz
   - iOS session at 96kHz
   - Bit-perfect playback

2. **LMS prefetches Track 2 (STRM command)**
   - Decoder created for 88.2kHz track
   - Format mismatch detected (96kHz stream vs 88.2kHz decoder)
   - Track 2 stored as `pendingTrack` (NOT started)
   - iOS session remains at 96kHz ✅
   - Track 1 continues undisturbed

3. **Track 1 finishes (buffer empties)**
   - `handleBufferEnd()` triggered
   - Calls `startDeferredTrack(pendingTrack)`

4. **Clean transition to Track 2**
   - `setPreferredSampleRate(88200)` called NOW
   - Old push stream freed
   - New push stream created at 88.2kHz
   - iOS session switches to 88.2kHz
   - Track 2 starts playing (bit-perfect at 88.2kHz)

### Testing Checklist

**Mixed Sample Rate Playlists:**
- [ ] 96kHz → 88.2kHz → 44.1kHz → 96kHz → 48kHz
- [ ] 192kHz → 96kHz → 48kHz → 44.1kHz
- [ ] 44.1kHz → 48kHz → 88.2kHz → 96kHz → 192kHz

**Expected Behavior:**
✅ Sample rate changes ONLY at track boundaries
✅ NO resampling during prefetching
✅ NO brief silence during playback (smooth transitions)
✅ DAC display shows correct rate throughout each track
✅ True gapless playback (no audio gap at transitions)

**Same Sample Rate Tracks:**
- [ ] All 96kHz tracks (no rate changes)
- [ ] All 44.1kHz tracks (no rate changes)
- [ ] Verify iOS session stays at same rate throughout

**Edge Cases:**
- [ ] Very short tracks (< 5 seconds) with rate changes
- [ ] Skip to next track during prefetch (pending track handling)
- [ ] Manual stop during prefetch (pendingTrack cleanup)

### Technical Implementation

**pendingTrack Mechanism:**
```swift
struct PendingTrackInfo {
    url: String
    format: String
    decoderStream: HSTREAM  // Keep HTTP connection alive!
    sampleRate: Int         // New track's rate
    channels: Int
}
```

**Key Code Locations:**
- `startDecodingFromURL()`: Detects format mismatch, stores pendingTrack (line 642-700)
- `handleBufferEnd()`: Triggers deferred track start (line 1373-1391)
- `startDeferredTrack()`: Changes iOS rate, recreates stream, starts track (line 1395-1452)
- `initializePushStream()`: Sets iOS sample rate via setPreferredSampleRate (line 354-395)

### Dependency Resolution

This fix resolves the gapless sample rate change mechanism. The task can be closed once testing confirms:
1. No premature resampling during prefetch
2. Clean transitions at track boundaries
3. Bit-perfect playback maintained throughout each track
4. Works with all sample rate combinations

title: Phase 6: Handle 401 Unauthorized responses gracefully
description:
Add graceful handling of HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses from LMS servers.

Implementation Details:
- Monitor BASS stream creation errors for HTTP 401
- Parse HTTP response codes from BASS error callbacks
- Show user-friendly alert when credentials are invalid
- Suggest checking username/password in settings
- Add retry mechanism with credential prompt
- Update connection test to validate authentication
- Log authentication failures for debugging

Error Messages:
- "Authentication failed. Please check username and password in Settings"
- "Server requires authentication. Please enter credentials in Server Configuration"

Files to Modify:
- LMS_StreamTest/AudioPlayer.swift (error handling)
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift (connection handling)
- LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift (connection test)

Dependencies:
- Requires AudioPlayer auth implementation (Phase 4)
notes:
Phase 6 may not be necessary with URL-embedded credentials approach.

REASON:
With URL-embedded credentials (http://user:pass@host/path), authentication happens at the HTTP protocol level BEFORE BASS gets the stream data. BASS doesn't expose HTTP status codes - it only reports "stream creation success" or "generic network failure."

WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE:
✅ WebView 401 Detection (Phase 5A) - ContentView.swift handles NSURLErrorDomain code -1012
✅ User-friendly error messages for WebView authentication failures
✅ Fallback settings button when WebView fails to load

STREAM URL BEHAVIOR:
- Correct credentials → BASS successfully creates stream → audio plays
- Wrong credentials → HTTP 401 → BASS fails stream creation with generic network error
- Cannot distinguish "401 auth failure" from "server down" or "network issue" at BASS level

BASS LIMITATIONS:
- BASS_StreamCreateURL() returns 0 on ANY network failure
- BASS_ErrorGetCode() returns generic error codes (not HTTP-specific)
- No HTTP response code exposure in BASS API
- URL-embedded auth is transparent to BASS (handled by HTTP layer)

CURRENT ERROR HANDLING:
AudioPlayer already logs stream creation failures:
- "Failed to create stream: [generic BASS error]"
- "Stream error detected: [error code]"
- These cover auth failures (they just look like network errors)

RECOMMENDATION:
Phase 6 implementation would require:
1. Custom HTTP layer to intercept 401 responses BEFORE passing to BASS
2. Significant architectural changes to AudioPlayer/SlimProtoCommandHandler
3. Complexity without clear user benefit (they'll see "stream failed" either way)

BETTER APPROACH:
1. Test Phase 7 with wrong credentials to see actual user experience
2. If stream failures with wrong auth are unclear, add guidance:
   "Stream failed to load. If your server requires authentication, check Settings."
3. Connection test in settings could validate auth before attempting playback

CONCLUSION:
Phase 6 as originally scoped (monitoring BASS errors for 401) is not feasible with URL-embedded credentials. The HTTP 401 happens below BASS's visibility. Consider Phase 6 complete via Phase 5A (WebView 401 handling), or rescope to add connection testing.

title: Hygiene sweep: dead code, unreachable branches, lying comments (audit checklist)
description:
Dead code and misleading comments found in the audit. Zero intended behavior change — pure deletion/correction. One PR, reviewed carefully.

CHECKLIST:
- AudioPlayer.configureForFormat (AudioPlayer.swift:1151-1194): all real config commented out, but logs still claim "FLAC configured with user settings: Xs buffer" / "1.5s playback, 50s network". Delete the method + call, or make logs truthful.
- AudioStreamDecoder decode loop: 100MB "soft throttle" (:1358-1373) is unreachable — the primary throttle (:1179) caps total buffer at 11.5MB. Its comment claims a 150MB hard limit; the actual BASS_ATTRIB_PUSH_LIMIT set is 50MB (:672). Delete the dead branch, fix the limit comment.
- trackJiffiesEpoch machinery (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:91-92, 1438-1467): jiffiesEpoch/jiffiesOffsetList written, never read; fed result["time"] (track POSITION, not a clock) so the math is meaningless; comments describe a "PHASE 1 player synchronization" that lives in SyncController instead. Delete.
- formatNameFromCType duplicated verbatim (AudioPlayer.swift:865-914 and AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1442-1491). Extract to one shared helper.
- sendJSONRPCCommand pause path (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1804-1815): 500ms asyncAfter "getting current server position first" fetches nothing (position already saved in sendLockScreenCommand). Remove the delay + comment; verify pause feels snappier.
- Empty asyncAfter bodies: SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:2343-2345, :2359-2361, connectionManagerDidReconnectAfterTimeout :2560-2567 (empty stub) + its misnamed trigger wasConnectedBeforeTimeout (SlimProtoConnectionManager.swift:54, fires on EVERY disconnect, not just timeouts).
- UserDefaults self-assignments (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:827, :1734).
- Write-only/dead state: wasDisconnectedWhileInBackground (:79/:833), backgroundedWhilePlaying (:78), startServerTimeSync/stopServerTimeSync log-only stubs, savePositionToServerPreferences (:1032-1071) writing prefs nothing reads; SlimProtoClient.swift:21-35 computed vars + :55-56 flags; SlimProtoCommandHandler streamPosition/streamDuration/lastStreamUpdate/serverStartTime/serverStartPosition (:26-32), unused isDirectStream local (:281); AudioManager lastTimeUpdateReport/minimumTimeUpdateInterval (:21-22).
- Comment fixes: SlimProtoClient.swift:269-272 says "device ID 9" twice, code sends 12 (12 is correct); SHUT/disconnectWithPositionSave comment (:145-170) claims a persist call that doesn't exist; AudioManager.audioStreamDecoderNeedsMoreData TODO (:699-703) promises a socket-fed data path that will never exist (audio flows over the decoder's own HTTP fetch).
- SimpleTimeTracker stale duration (SimpleTimeTracker.swift:34-37): duration only overwritten when > 0, so a radio stream after a track keeps the old track's duration. Reset on stream change.
- ensureSlimProtoConnection (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:2323-2363): can stack overlapping connects + spawns a new 1s repeating timer per call. Guard with the connection manager's state and a single timer.

TEST GATE: build + full unit suite both platforms; one device smoke session (play/pause/skip/lock screen).
