title: BASS_SYNC_END data!=0 filter is a no-op (misread docs) — premature-end guard doesn't guard
description:
PROBLEM: AudioPlayer's BASS_SYNC_END callback (AudioPlayer.swift:1011-1029) treats data != 0 as "network/stream issue - ignoring (fixes cellular FLAC premature skipping)". Per BASS docs (BASS_ChannelSetSync, verified in docs/bass_documentation): for BASS_SYNC_END, data=1 means a MOD-music backward jump, 2 = BASS_POS_END position, 3 = tail end — NONE of which occur for HTTP audio streams. A dropped connection still ends with data=0, so this filter does not prevent premature track-end on cellular; the claimed fix is a no-op and the comment misleads.

FIX (legacy URL-stream path only): decide what premature-end protection should actually look like — e.g. on SYNC_END, compare BASS_StreamGetFilePosition(BASS_FILEPOS_END/DOWNLOAD) or elapsed-vs-metadata-duration; if clearly short of the track duration, treat as a stall/error (retry or STMn) instead of natural end. At minimum, correct the comment so future readers don't trust the filter.

TEST: legacy-path (HTTP mode) track allowed to finish → exactly one natural track end. If implementing short-end detection: kill the stream source mid-track → app must not report a clean track end to the server.
acceptance_criteria: Comment/logic reflect actual BASS_SYNC_END semantics; decision recorded on real premature-end handling for the legacy path
close_reason: Closed

title: lyrplay_recovery_index has four racing writers — recovery can jump to the previous track
description:
PROBLEM: lyrplay_recovery_index (UserDefaults) has four writers that can diverge: (1) local increment at gapless boundary (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1357-1361), (2) overwrite from the 3s server-time poll (parseServerTimeResponse ~:1630-1635), (3) saveCurrentPositionForRecovery (:554), (4) no-op self-assignments (:827, :1734). Failure: a poll response that left the server BEFORE a boundary lands AFTER the local increment → index rewinds → next recovery playlist-jumps to the previous track.

FIX: single writer discipline. Prefer server-derived index but reject stale writes: tag the local increment with a timestamp and ignore poll-derived values older than the last boundary; or only accept poll values when they move forward/match. Delete the self-assignments.

TEST: play across a gapless boundary then immediately kill the server (before next poll) → recovery must jump to the NEW track index, not the previous one.
acceptance_criteria: Recovery index has one authoritative update path; boundary-then-disconnect recovers to the correct track

title: First push stream hardcoded 44100/2 — recreate churn on every hi-res first track
description:
PROBLEM: the first push stream of a session is hardcoded to 44100Hz/2ch (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:1168 → AudioManager.startPushStreamPlayback defaults). Every session whose first track is 48k/96k content takes the format-mismatch recreate path inside startDecodingFromURL (:960-1007): create stream at 44.1k, detect mismatch, free, recreate, plus an AVAudioSession preferred-rate change — wasted work and extra session churn at the most latency-sensitive moment.

FIX: don't create the push stream until the decoder stream reports the actual format; initializePushStream directly at the real rate/channels. (The decoder already opens first and knows info.freq/chans before any data is pushed.) Alternatively pass the STRM pcm fields when the server provides them.

TEST: first track of a fresh launch at 48kHz starts without a "Format mismatch! Recreating push stream" log; time-to-first-audio unchanged or better; 44.1k first track regression-free.
acceptance_criteria: Push stream created at the decoder's actual rate on first track; no mismatch-recreate on session start

title: Deferred-track start can fire early: buffer stall from network underrun mistaken for track end
description:
PROBLEM: deferred-track start (format-mismatch gapless) is triggered by BASS_SYNC_STALL with data=0 = "buffer empty" (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:22-35, handleBufferEnd :1667-1685). The design assumes stall == current track finished playing. But STALL also fires on a mid-track network underrun. If a pendingTrack is queued (next track has different sample rate) and a >30s cellular dead spot drains the buffer mid-track, handleBufferEnd starts the deferred track EARLY — truncating the remainder of the current track.

FIX: in handleBufferEnd, only start the pending track if the current track's decode has actually completed (decoder loop finished naturally / decoderStream==0 and not mid-download). If decode is still in progress, treat as an underrun: wait for data (BASS resumes automatically) and keep pendingTrack queued.

TEST: hard to reproduce live — simulate by pausing the LMS transcode process / throttling network while a mismatched-rate next track is queued; current track must resume, not jump.
acceptance_criteria: Mid-track underrun with a pending format-mismatch track queued resumes the current track instead of starting the next one

title: STMl threshold compares cumulative bytes — fires instantly for every gapless track
description:
PROBLEM: the STMl buffer-ready check uses CUMULATIVE totalBytesPushed (AudioStreamDecoder.swift:1385: !sentSTMl && totalBytesPushed >= bufferReadyThreshold). totalBytesPushed is deliberately cumulative across gapless tracks (never reset), so for every track after the first, the threshold is already exceeded → STMl fires on the FIRST chunk instead of after ~2s of buffered audio. Mostly masked (gapless tracks use autostart '1' where STMl is informational) but wrong for any wait-for-unpause track that reuses the stream.

FIX: track bytes-pushed-for-current-track (e.g. totalBytesPushed - trackStartWriteOffset captured when the track's decode begins) and compare THAT against bufferReadyThreshold.

TEST: sync-group start of a second track (autostart '0'): STMl appears in LMS log ~2s of audio after decode start, not instantly.
acceptance_criteria: STMl fires when ~2s of the CURRENT track is buffered; sync-group unpause handshake regression-free

title: audg ignores right-channel gain
description:
PROBLEM: processVolumeCommand (SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:679-700) reads only new_gainL (bytes 10..<14) and ignores new_gainR (14..<18). Server-side balance or channel-specific gain is dropped. squeezelite applies both gains per channel.

FIX: parse both; BASS has a single channel volume, so apply e.g. max(L,R) or their average for overall level (document the choice) — or use BASS_ChannelSetAttribute with a BASS_FX/mixer matrix if true per-channel gain is ever wanted (probably overkill; note it and move on).

TEST: set balance hard-left/hard-right in LMS → app volume behaves sanely (documented behavior); normal volume slider unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Both gains parsed; documented mapping to BASS volume; server volume slider regression-free

title: Duplicate STAT replies (STMt/STMp x2 per poll, double STMr/STMf)
description:
PROBLEM: duplicate STAT replies. Every strm 't' poll is answered twice: coordinator's didReceiveStatusRequest path sends STMt/STMp WITHOUT the timestamp echo (SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:~1409-1424), then the command handler also sends STMt/STMp WITH it (SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:577-585). Same duplication: STMr sent on resume by both handler (:529) and coordinator (:1284); STMf sent on stop/flush by both (:539/:549 and coordinator :1316). LMS uses the timestamp echo for playPoint/RTT in sync groups; an extra timestamp-less STAT every poll is protocol noise that perturbs sync math and doubles STAT volume.

FIX: one owner per STAT. Keep the handler's timestamped reply for 't'; make the coordinator's didReceiveStatusRequest do bookkeeping only. De-dupe STMr/STMf the same way (pick the handler as the protocol-reply owner; the coordinator owns lifecycle-driven STATs like STMd/STMs).

TEST: LMS log (--debug network.protocol.slimproto) or packet capture: exactly one STAT per 't' poll, timestamp echoed; one STMr per unpause; one STMf per stop.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one STAT per server event, with correct timestamp echo, verified in LMS protocol log

title: Format-accept check runs for every strm command, not just 's'
description:
PROBLEM: processServerCommand (SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:185-264) runs the format-accept switch for EVERY strm command and sends STMn + returns on rejection BEFORE dispatching on the command byte. This only works because LMS hardcodes format byte 'm' into all non-'s' frames (slimserver Squeezebox.pm sub stream). Any server/fork that packs a different filler byte would make the client answer every status poll with a decode-error STMn (which LMS treats as track failure).

FIX: move format validation inside the 's' (start) case only; 't'/'p'/'u'/'a'/'q'/'f' must not consult the format byte. (squeezelite only parses format in its 's' handler.)

TEST: unit test: a strm 't' with format byte 0x00 must produce STMt, not STMn. Device: normal playback + status polls regression.
acceptance_criteria: Non-'s' strm commands ignore the format byte; unit test with unknown format byte on 't' passes
close_reason: Format rejection gated on streamCommand=='s' via pure rejectsFormat helper; 5 unit tests incl. 't' with format 0x00 not rejected (reaches STMt dispatch) and all non-'s' commands ignoring the byte. Both platforms green.

title: strm 't' timestamp read from server_ip field instead of replay_gain (latent)
description:
PROBLEM: handleStatusRequest (SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift:552-563) extracts the strm 't' server timestamp from bytes 20..<24 — that's the server_ip field of the 'aaaaaaaCCCaCCCNnN' strm layout. The timestamp squeezelite echoes lives in the replay_gain field at bytes 14..<18 (squeezelite/slimproto.c:285: sendSTAT("STMt", strm->replay_gain)). Masked today because modern LMS sends 0 in both fields for 't' (Squeezebox.pm: "stop using this method to track latency"), but the offset and the comment ("bytes 20-23") are simply wrong and will bite against any server/fork that repopulates it.

FIX: read 14..<18 (the replayGainFixed already extracted at :169-170 IS the right value — just use it); fix the comment.

TEST: unit test on a synthetic 't' payload with a nonzero replay_gain field → STAT echoes it. No device behavior change expected with current LMS.
acceptance_criteria: Timestamp echoed from bytes 14-17; unit test covers nonzero timestamp
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 5: Hygiene sweep (dead code, lying comments)
description:
Dead code and misleading-comment sweep. Zero behavior change intended — the gate is purely regression.

DEVICE TEST GATE:
- Build + full unit suite on both platforms; one normal-playback smoke session on device.

title: iOS sim: 3 PlaybackSessionControllerTests fail on iOS 26 runtime (interruption + CarPlay route change)
description: Pre-existing on tvos-target (verified on unmodified working tree, iPhone 17 / iOS 26 simulator): testCarPlayRouteChangeTriggersConnectAndPause, testInterruptionFromOtherAudioDoesNotAutoResume, testInterruptionPausesAndResumesWhenIndicated fail; other 11 in the suite pass (136 tests pass overall). Suspect iOS 26 AVAudioSession notification behavior change on simulator rather than product code — needs xcresult inspection. Found while verifying the CLAUDE.md iOS test command.

Failed on every runtime, not just iOS 26 (proof: XCTAssertEqual pauseCount/playCount 0 != 1, connectCalled false, savedPosition false — none of which the current handlers touch). Rewrote the 3 tests to assert current server-command behavior (commandsSent). Full iOS suite now green. CLAUDE.md note corrected.

title: tvOS UITests runner fails to load (dlopen can't find CocoaAsyncSocket.framework) — masks unit-test results in xcodebuild test
description: xcodebuild test -scheme LMS_StreamTest-tvOS reports ** TEST FAILED ** even when all unit tests pass, because the LMS_StreamTest-tvOSUITests runner bundle can't dlopen CocoaAsyncSocket.framework on the simulator. Breaks CI-style verification (must use -only-testing:LMS_StreamTest-tvOSTests as a workaround). Found during pilot iteration on 98q.13.

title: tvOS SearchResultsModel.reset() doesn't rotate cancellation token — in-flight responses survive a query clear
description: Pre-existing behavior preserved verbatim in the 98q.13 extraction (SearchResultsModel.swift reset()). Clear query mid-flight then retype within the 500ms debounce window: the cleared query's late responses pass the token guard and repopulate results + set hasFetched. Fix is one line: rotate lastQueryToken = UUID() in reset(). Found by adversarial review of pilot/LMS_StreamTest-98q.13; test scaffolding for it already exists in SearchResultsModelTests.

title: Evaluate native safe-area inset vs JS topPad machinery in ContentView
description:
After the CarPlay WebView mis-sizing fix, ContentView has ~4 topPad injection sites (didCommit :889, didFinish :934, 1s verify :946, scenePhase==.active) plus an orientation observer — all fighting one problem: Material draws its toolbar behind the iOS status bar, so we push interactive elements down via a JS --top-pad CSS var + queryParams.topPad.

First-principles alternative: stop .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges:[.top]) on the WebView (ContentView.swift:160) and let SwiftUI/UIKit apply the top safe-area inset natively, deleting most of the topPad JS dance.

Risk: Material expects to paint its toolbar background behind the status bar; native inset would leave a gap there unless Material is told to extend its background. Needs a spike to confirm Material renders acceptably with a native inset before committing. Out of scope for the activation-bug fix (PR that created this issue). Revisit when touching this area again.

title: Convert large tuples to named structs (readability cleanup)
description:
SwiftLint large_tuple findings. Low-risk, compiler-verified, no device test needed. Convert these 3+-field return tuples to named structs:

- CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:498 — 7-field per-row tuple (title, artist, duration, playlistIndex, trackID, coverID, isCurrentTrack) in displayUpNextQueue(). Biggest win → make a UpNextItem struct.
- NowPlayingManager.swift:152 — (time, isPlaying, source) from getCurrentPlaybackInfo()
- NowPlayingManager.swift:204 — (position, wasPlaying, isValid) from getStoredPositionWithTimeOffset(); unlabeled call sites like 'return (0.0, false, false)' are error-prone
- SettingsView.swift:886
- LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/ManualServerEntryView.swift:178

Context: came out of a SwiftLint audit (2026-05-30). Audit conclusion: core audio/protocol code (processServerCommand complexity 42, startDecoderLoop complexity 25) is honest complexity / faithful squeezelite ports — leave alone. These tuples are the one genuinely safe readability improvement. Build verifies correctness; no automated tests exist so audio/protocol code stays hands-off.

title: tvOS: built-in album shelves play immediately on Select, no drill into the track list
description: mherger build-11 round-4: 'the built-in stuff like Random Albums would not allow me to drill down to the track level, but would immediately play the album.' Built-in album shelves (HomeExtraShelf .albums case -> playAlbum -> playlistcontrol cmd:load album_id) play the whole album on Select with no path to the album's track list. Not a regression (always behaved this way) — an enhancement + a consistency point: built-in album shelves play-on-Select while plugin shelves drill-on-Select, so the interaction model is inconsistent. Consider in the round-4 /office-hours on the overall interaction model.
close_reason: Fixed in tvOS build 12 (07d87d0 round-4 interaction fixes; 51c in efb1696 with tests). Code-verified: Menu pops one level (HomeExtraShelvesView), Select fires goAction (JiveBrowseView), BuiltinTrackListView drill-down exists, repairingMojibake in parseRegistry. No re-report from mherger through build 21.

title: tvOS: nextWindow:nowplaying auto-selects the Now Playing tab
description: Deferred from the build-11 7do SlimBrowse rebuild (eng review 2026-05-21). When a JiveBrowse action returns nextWindow:nowplaying, build 11 only dismisses the .fullScreenCover back to Library. Auto-selecting the Now Playing tab needs a TabView selection binding threaded ContentView->LibraryView->HomeExtraShelvesView->JiveBrowseView. Held back because it touches the app top-level navigation contract and interacts with the 98q.5 MPRemoteCommandCenter invariant in ContentView. Depends on 7do.
notes: Closed not-wanted (2026-05-22). mherger's round-4 feedback explicitly described wanting to stay in browse hierarchy ('I'd always end up in the Home again, from where I have to start the navigation over' — he wanted the album level, not Now Playing). Today's nextWindow:nowplaying behavior already dismisses the cover; auto-switching the tab on top of that would fight the user's stated mental model. Re-open if a user reports wanting auto-switch to Now Playing — until then, the Now Playing tab is one tap away when wanted.
close_reason: Closed

title: tvOS: localise native UI strings (String Catalog)
description:
mherger round 3 (forum post 1823551). LyrPlay tvOS native UI strings are hard-coded English. mherger (LMS maintainer, German locale) flagged that even built-in shelf names render English when Material localises them.

Two distinct buckets:
- Built-in shelf names + all native-view strings ('New Music', 'Recently Played', 'Library is empty', 'Search music', shelf subtitles, Settings labels, etc.) — these are OUR strings. Need a String Catalog (.xcstrings) + String(localized:). LibraryShelf.title/.subtitle in PlaylistModels.swift is the main catalog; plus the tvOS views.
- Plugin shelf titles — already localised server-side by LMS (Slim::Utils::Strings::getString in Plugin.pm). We just render what we get; no work needed beyond the mojibake fix (51c).

Scope decision for /office-hours: which languages, where the catalog lives (shared vs tvOS-only target), whether to ship German first (mherger can review), and whether iOS native strings are in scope (most of iOS is Material's WebView, so likely tvOS-only). Opus can factor the strings out mechanically once scope is set.
acceptance_criteria: tvOS native UI renders localised on a German LMS / German Apple TV. String Catalog in place. Built-in shelf names match Material's German.
close_reason: Shipped: German localization build 11 + PR #87 wording refinements.

title: tvOS: CometD long-poll subscriber for live home-screen updates (Approach C scope)
description:
Deferred from Approach B (medium scope) decision in /office-hours 2026-05-19. Build 9 ships .onAppear + lastscan compare; live updates require this work.

Reference mechanism (verified against Material's lms-material at HEAD pulled 2026-05-19):
- server.js:437-455 subscribes to CometD channels /slim/serverstatus, /slim/favorites, /slim/playerstatus, /slim/playerprefs, /slim/serverprefs, /slim/material-skin
- On any serverstatus message: compare data.lastscan against lmsLastScan; if changed, clearListCache()
- On scan-progress in progress: poll every 2s, on completion fire bus.$emit('refreshList', SECTION_NEWMUSIC) + refresh release types + refreshServerStatus
- 500ms debounce on home-refresh and favorites-refresh

Implementation scope:
- CometD long-poll HTTP client (no library exists for Swift; ~300-500 LOC)
- Channel subscription state machine (suspend on background, reconnect on resume)
- tvOS app lifecycle integration (Scene phase change → suspend/resume CometD)
- Existing LibraryView fetch becomes reactive: subscribe on appear, observe lastscan changes, refetch without serverstatus probe
- Same machinery enables live favorites updates and player events the SlimProto channel doesn't carry

Effort: ~1-2 weeks human / multiple CC sessions
Dependencies: build 9 (this design doc) lands first

Design doc: /Users/ericmiller/.gstack/projects/LMS_StreamTest/ericmiller-tvos-target-design-20260519-055206.md (Approach C section)
acceptance_criteria: Library tab shows new albums within ~2 seconds of LMS scan completing, no .onAppear needed. New favorites added from another LMS controller appear in real time. tvOS suspend/resume cycles cleanly reconnect; no zombie connections after background return.

title: tvOS: Jive add/more action support in JiveBrowseView
description: SUPERSEDED by LMS_StreamTest-7do — the Jive interaction-model rebuild covers add/more actions as part of the full go/play/add/nextWindow dispatch model. Keep open as a sub-concern or close in favour of 7do after the office-hours design lands.

title: tvOS Now Playing: typography polish to match iPhone Material (Elissen #2)
description:
## Source
GitHub issue #83 (Elissen, 2026-05-11) round 1 tvOS feedback. Design doc:
`~/.gstack/projects/LMS_StreamTest/ericmiller-tvos-target-design-20260515-053612.md`

## Symptoms (vs iPhone Material UI)

1. **Spacing too tight.** On tvOS the title/artist/album block sits flush against
   the tech-info line; iPhone has breathing room between them.
2. **Tech-info text is too large.** "FLAC • 48kHz • 24-bit • Stereo @ 0 kbps"
   reads as primary content on tvOS — should be secondary/caption-level.
3. **Drop "Stereo @" prefix.** iPhone shows just "1303kbps" alongside the
   format/sample-rate; tvOS shows "Stereo @ 0 kbps" which adds noise.

## Files

- `LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/NowPlayingView.swift` — metadata column layout.

## Notes

- "Stereo @" drop is already covered in the Item 4 (progress bar) work in
  the design doc — those edits can land in the same PR. The font size and
  spacing changes are independent and lower priority.
- Italian/Dutch/German renderers may want narrower spacing if/when
  localization (Elissen #7) lands — design for tightenable spacing rather
  than hardcoded values.

title: Add snapshot-test infra for tvOS view layer - auto-catch TVScreen/TVList regressions
Untrack xcuserdata/ and add to .gitignore
description:
Xcode user-specific files at LMS_StreamTest.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/ericmiller.xcuserdatad/ and Pods/Pods.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/ericmiller.xcuserdatad/ are tracked in git. These are per-developer Xcode state (scheme order, last-used scheme, breakpoints, window layouts) and don't belong in version control — they cause noise diffs whenever you open Xcode and produce false-positive merge conflicts.

Surfaced during the pre-merge audit on the tvos-target branch (commits 26595d7 → 3bf1036): the xcschememanagement.plist diff churned just from adding the tvOS scheme, contributing nothing meaningful to the change.

Recommended fix:
  1. Add to .gitignore (project root):
       xcuserdata/
       *.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/
       Pods/Pods.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/
  2. git rm -r --cached LMS_StreamTest.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/
  3. git rm -r --cached Pods/Pods.xcodeproj/xcuserdata/
  4. Commit. Xcode will re-create the directory locally on next open but it'll be ignored.

Pre-existing condition (already in main); not a new exposure from the tvOS work. Low priority cleanup — defer until the next time someone is doing repo hygiene work, or if you ever onboard a second developer who would otherwise see your xcschememanagement.plist diffs polluting their checkout.

title: URL credential injection: special chars in password break artwork URLs
description:
## Surfaced during 98q.9 /review (2026-05-06)

`LMSArtworkURL.cover(...)` and `LMSArtworkURL.favoriteIcon(...)` (LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/LMSArtworkURL.swift:26-30 and 60-64) inject credentials via `URLComponents.user` and `.password` assignment.

Per Apple docs, `URLComponents.user` and `.password` setters require the value to be already percent-encoded. LMS users with special characters in their password (legal: `@`, `:`, `/`, `?`, `#`, `&`, etc) silently break: either the URL ends up nil, or the credential lands incorrectly and artwork fetches return 401.

This affects:
- Library tab artwork (Favorites icons, Recently Played album covers, New Music covers)
- Queue artwork
- ANY future caller of LMSArtworkURL

Same code shape exists pre-98q.9 in `SettingsManager.injectCredentialsIntoURL` (line 717-743) used by NowPlayingManager artwork fetch — likely affected too.

## Repro

1. LMS server with auth enabled, password contains `@` (e.g. `mypass@123`)
2. tvOS app connects and tries to load artwork
3. Artwork shows placeholder; URL likely came back nil from URLComponents

## Related to but separate from
- `LMS_StreamTest-7e4` — credentials embedded in URL leak via cache keys + http wire (privacy concern). The fix for -7e4 (move to Authorization header) would also fix THIS bug. Could be bundled.

## Fix (when bundled with -7e4)

Replace inline credential URL composition with custom URLSession that adds `Authorization: Basic <base64>` header. Same pattern `NowPlayingManager.loadArtwork` already uses (NowPlayingManager.swift:278-281). Affects `LMSArtworkURL.swift` + `SettingsManager.injectCredentialsIntoURL`. AsyncImage doesn't natively support custom URLSession — need to wrap with our own image loader (cleanest fix solves -ppz too).

## Affected files
- `LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/LMSArtworkURL.swift` (98q.9 helper)
- `LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift:717-743` (existing pre-98q.9 helper)
- `LMS_StreamTest/NowPlayingManager.swift:278-281` (correct pattern reference)

## Out of 98q.9 scope
Filed as P3 — affects auth-only setups with special-char passwords (small population). Bundle the fix with -7e4 + -ppz when shared image loader is built.
acceptance_criteria: Artwork URLs work correctly when LMS password contains @, :, /, ?, #, &, or unicode. Verified by setting a known-bad-char password on test LMS instance and confirming Library + Now Playing artwork loads.

title: tvOS: Visualizer customization options (TBD presets, settings, tunables)
description:
## Context

Initial visualizer (98q.7) shipped a single Metal radial-bloom polar shader with hardcoded tuning constants. Per discussion at end of 98q.7 step 2 commit, user has ideas to improve / customize the visualizer experience that should land as a separate ticket once scope is firmed up.

## Tunables that exist today (any of these could become user-configurable)

VisualizerEngine.swift:
- visualGain (12.0) — band amplification before sqrt compression
- visualCeiling (2.0) — pre-sqrt cap
- riseFactor (0.40) / fallFactor (0.85) — asymmetric smoothing
- bandCount (renderer-side, 64) — angular resolution / shader sampling

VisualizerShaders.metal:
- petalR base / range (0.30 + v*0.40) — bloom size + amplitude response
- ring sharpness (32.0 in exp falloff) — petal edge softness
- core / halo strengths (0.6/0.05) — center glow + outer falloff
- time rotation rate (0.05) — how fast the bloom rotates
- aspect handling — assumes ~16:9 widescreen

VisualizerView.swift:
- drawableSize (1920×1080) — render resolution before system upscale

NowPlayingView.swift:
- accent extraction — currently CIAreaAverage; could expose 'use artwork color / fixed brand palette / per-frame FFT-derived' choice

## Scope ideas for this ticket (pick a subset, TBD)

1. **Multiple shader presets** — radial bloom (current), spectrum bars, particle field, plasma/raymarched. UI to switch between them (Settings? Long-press while overlay is up?).
2. **Color palette modes** — artwork accent (current), fixed brand, per-frame FFT-derived (gimmicky risk — was rejected for v1 in plan-eng-review D5 but worth exploring for power-user mode).
3. **Idle auto-engage** — N seconds of remote idle on Now Playing fades into visualizer (LMS Material Skin pattern; was option C in plan-eng-review D2, rejected for v1).
4. **Sensitivity / responsiveness controls** — gain, smoothing, etc. exposed as user-tunable sliders. Dangerous (easy to break aesthetic) but flexible.
5. **Per-album visualizer choice** — remembered preset per album / artist / genre.

## Out of scope (still v2+ even if this ticket lands)

- Native 4K rendering (drawable stays 1080p per 98q.7 D6; revisit only if perf headroom permits)
- ATV HD support (TVOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET still cuts off A8 hardware)
- Milkdrop / ProjectM preset import (massive scope; would be its own multi-week project)

## When to schedule

Not blocking 98q.8 (Search) or 98q.9 (Favorites). Visualizer is functional today; this is taste / polish work that benefits from real listening-session feedback before scoping. Recommend deferring until after TestFlight beta (kua) when actual users have used it for a few sessions and have specific complaints / wishes.
notes:
Design doc approved 2026-05-16 via /office-hours: scoped to 4 presets (bloom + LED hi-fi + Winamp + iTunes-clean), bloom+bar uber-shader architecture (Approach B), click-pad LEFT/RIGHT switcher, palette baked per preset. Sliders / idle auto-engage / per-album memory explicitly deferred to v2. Step 0 kill-switch: throwaway-branch LED feel-check + Siri Remote gen-1 .onMoveCommand reliability test BEFORE full build. title: tvOS Queue: artwork URL leaks credentials in URL line
description: QueueView.artworkURL embeds activeServerUsername/Password in URLComponents (http://user:pass@host/...). On http (cleartext) and through proxies, this exposes credentials in URL caches, server access logs, and Referer headers. AsyncImage uses URLSession.shared so the cred-bearing URL becomes the cache key. Acceptable for v1 home-LAN deployments; real concern for remote/hosted LMS. Fix: build URL without userinfo and attach Authorization: Basic via URLSessionConfiguration.urlCredentialStorage with URLProtectionSpace, mirroring how generateAuthHeader() is used elsewhere. Or replace AsyncImage with a small custom view that uses URLRequest.

title: tvOS Queue: tap-to-jump failure overlay
description: tvOS QueueView's tap-to-jump path (sendJSONRPCCommandDirect with ["playlist", "index", N]) currently logs failures silently. Add a brief overlay (e.g. .ultraThinMaterial pill: 'Couldn't switch tracks') with ~1-2s auto-dismiss on RPC empty-response or error. ~1 hr of work; not blocking 98q.6 ship.

title: tvOS Queue: refresh on web-UI queue reorder via SlimProto subscribe
description: tvOS QueueView (98q.6) refreshes only on .onAppear and on .onChange(currentTrackTitle). When a user reorders the LMS playlist from the web UI without changing the currently playing track, the tvOS Queue list stays stale until the next track event. Fix: subscribe to LMS player JSON-RPC notifications and re-fetch the playlist when queue mutations arrive. Alternative: pull-to-refresh gesture (Siri Remote menu long-press or up-swipe). Either is acceptable. See 98q.6 plan-eng-review test plan for the exact gap.

title: tvOS: player name shows hardcoded 'iOS Player' instead of UIDevice.current.name
description:
On tvOS, HELO sends player name 'iOS Player' instead of 'Apple TV' (UIDevice.current.name fallback).

## Root cause
SettingsManager.swift:154 sets playerName = 'iOS Player' on first init, BEFORE the effectivePlayerName fallback at L573 can fire UIDevice.current.name. Same hardcoded default lives at L524 (regenerate path) and L573 (final fallback).

## Files
- LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift:154 (first-init default)
- LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift:524 (regenerate path)
- LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift:573 (final fallback)
- LMS_StreamTest/SettingsManager.swift:559-573 (effectivePlayerName logic)

## Repro
1. Install tvOS app on Apple TV
2. Configure server, observe in LMS Material UI -> player picker
3. Sees 'iOS Player' instead of device name

## Pre-existing
This bug ships on iOS too (where users typically rename in Settings). Just more visible on tvOS where the default device name 'Apple TV' would actually be useful.

## Surfaced during
98q.4a (LMS_StreamTest-6ki) end-to-end verification, 2026-05-05
close_reason: Resolved by 98q.7 step 2: SettingsManager.defaultPlayerName is now platform-aware ('tvOS Player' on tvOS, 'iOS Player' on iOS) at all 3 sites (init default, resetConfiguration, effectivePlayerName fallback).

title: Server discovery UDP broadcast misses non-standard subnets (e.g. 192.168.9.x)
description:
Reported in GitHub issue #76 follow-up (user ChristianNoc).

ServerDiscoveryManager.performUDPDiscovery() at ServerDiscoveryManager.swift:128-133
broadcasts to a hardcoded subnet list:
  - 255.255.255.255 (global, often filtered by routers/iOS)
  - 192.168.1.255
  - 192.168.0.255
  - 10.0.0.255

User's weekend network is 192.168.9.x — not in the list. Discovery returns nothing
even though the LMS server is reachable on the local subnet (music plays fine via
manual IP entry).

Fix direction: enumerate local interfaces with getifaddrs(), derive the actual
subnet broadcast address per interface (IP & netmask → broadcast), send the
discovery packet to each. Covers any subnet the device is on, no hardcoded list.

Unrelated to the backup server / failover fix in build 19. Independent of bug #76
body (that one is now fixed).

title: tvOS: Investigate and plan Apple TV app port
description:
Investigate feasibility of porting LyrPlay to tvOS (Apple TV).

## Platform Assessment

### What Works on tvOS
- SwiftUI (native support)
- CocoaAsyncSocket (networking)
- MPNowPlayingInfoCenter / MPRemoteCommandCenter
- URLSession for JSON-RPC
- UserDefaults, Keychain

### What Doesn't Work on tvOS
- **WebKit/WKWebView** - NOT available (no Material skin embedding)
- **CarPlay templates** - CarPlay-specific, won't work
- Touch-based UI - tvOS uses focus-based navigation (Siri Remote)

### Blockers to Investigate
1. **BASS audio library** - Need tvOS-compiled .a files from un4seen
   - Contact Ian at un4seen.com forum to request tvOS builds
   - Alternative: AVAudioEngine (more work, less codec support)

2. **Native Browse UI Required** - Can't use Material WebView
   - Need SwiftUI views for: Artists, Albums, Playlists, Search, Now Playing
   - Must support focus-based navigation (Siri Remote)

## Reusability Estimate

| Component | Reusable | Notes |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| SlimProtoClient | ✅ 100% | Protocol layer unchanged |
| SlimProtoCoordinator | ✅ 90% | Remove iOS-specific bits |
| AudioPlayer/BASS | ⚠️ 80% | Need tvOS BASS libs |
| SettingsManager | ✅ 90% | Minor adjustments |
| JSON-RPC browse calls | ✅ 100% | Already have the logic |
| NowPlayingManager | ✅ 80% | Similar on tvOS |
| WebView/Material UI | ❌ 0% | Must rebuild natively |
| CarPlay UI | ❌ 0% | CarPlay-specific |

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Feasibility
- [ ] Request tvOS BASS builds from un4seen

### Phase 2: Audio Playback

title: Add HTTPS support for server connections
description:
App currently hardcodes http:// for all server URLs. Users with reverse proxy setups (Caddy, nginx) cannot use HTTPS connections.

**Files requiring changes (12 URL locations + 2 UI locations):**

1. SettingsManager.swift (2 locations)
   - Line 406: testHTTPConnection()
   - Line 549: webURL computed property

2. SlimProtoCoordinator.swift (6 locations)
   - Line 1268: sendJSONRPCCommand()
   - Line 1559: sendPlaylistJumpCommand()
   - Line 1615: sendPlayPauseCommand()
   - Line 1744: fetchCurrentMetadata()
   - Line 1798-1800: artwork URL construction

3. SlimProtoCommandHandler.swift (1 location)
   - Line 600: stream URL construction

4. ServerDiscoveryManager.swift (1 location)
   - Line 50: server validation

5. CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift (2 locations)
   - Line 753: artwork URL
   - Line 1408: artwork URL

6. **OnboardingViews.swift** (UI)
   - ServerSetupView: Add HTTPS toggle to onboarding flow

7. **SettingsView.swift** (UI)
   - Server configuration section: Add HTTPS toggle

**Implementation Plan:**

Step 1: Add settings properties
- Add `useHTTPS: Bool = false` to SettingsManager
- Add `backupServerUseHTTPS: Bool = false` for backup server
- Add computed property `activeServerUseHTTPS`
- Add `urlScheme: String` computed property (returns "https" or "http")
- Add UserDefaults persistence for new properties

Step 2: Create URL builder helper
- Add `buildServerURL(path: String) -> String` method in SettingsManager
- Handles scheme, host, port, and path construction
- Centralizes URL building logic

Step 3: Update all URL constructions
- Replace all 12 hardcoded http:// constructions with helper method
- Keep artwork URL logic that checks hasPrefix("http")

Step 4: Add UI toggle - Onboarding
- Add HTTPS toggle in OnboardingViews.swift ServerSetupView
- Place in "Advanced" section near Authentication

Step 5: Add UI toggle - Settings
- Add HTTPS toggle in SettingsView server configuration
- Add for both primary and backup server settings

Step 6: Certificate handling (optional/future)
- Consider adding option to trust self-signed certificates
- May need custom URLSession delegate for cert validation

GitHub issue #31 (achurak's comment)
notes:
**Important Limitation:** SlimProto uses raw TCP sockets (port 3483), not HTTP. Standard reverse proxies (Caddy, nginx) only handle HTTP(S). Even with HTTPS support added, users would still need direct TCP access to LMS port 3483 for the SlimProto control connection. This significantly limits the value of HTTPS support for reverse proxy use cases.

Options for users wanting full reverse proxy:
1. Expose port 3483 directly alongside HTTPS proxy
2. Use TCP-capable proxy (nginx stream{}, HAProxy)
3. Use VPN/Tailscale for direct LMS access (already works)

title: Fix App Store warning: Missing 152x152 alternate icon for iPad
description:
## App Store Connect Warning

**Warning ID:** 90892
**Severity:** Non-blocking (app still works, just a recommendation)

### Full Warning Text:
```
Missing recommended icon. The bundle does not contain an alternate app icon for 
iPad of exactly '152x152' pixels, in .png format for iOS versions >= 10.0. To 
support older operating systems, the icon may be required in the bundle outside 
of an asset catalog. Make sure the Info.plist file includes appropriate entries 
referencing the file.
```

**Reference:** https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information_property_list/cfbundleicons

### Current Setup

We have 11 alternate icons, each with:
- ✅ 120x120 @2x PNG files (for iPhone)
- ✅ Asset catalog .appiconset folders (1024x1024 source)
- ✅ Info.plist CFBundleAlternateIcons entries

**Missing:**
- ❌ 152x152 PNG files (iPad @2x size for 76pt icon)
- ❌ 167x167 PNG files (iPad Pro @2x size for 83.5pt icon)

### Why It's Missing

iOS alternate icons documentation shows iPhone typically uses 60pt icons (120x120 @2x).
iPad uses 76pt icons (152x152 @2x) and iPad Pro uses 83.5pt icons (167x167 @2x).

We only created 120x120 files for iPhone testing.

### Solution Options

**Option A: Add iPad-specific icon sizes (Recommended)**

For each of the 11 alternate icons, create:
1. 152x152 PNG (iPad @2x)
2. 167x167 PNG (iPad Pro @2x)

Files needed:
- AppIcon-Gradient@2x~ipad.png (152x152)
- AppIcon-Gradient@3x~ipad.png (167x167)
- AppIcon-HiFi@2x~ipad.png (152x152)
- AppIcon-HiFi@3x~ipad.png (167x167)
- ... (repeat for all 11 icons)

Total: 22 additional files

**Option B: Let iOS scale from 120x120 (Current)**

- App works fine, just a warning
- iOS scales 120x120 to 152x152 automatically
- Not ideal for image quality but acceptable

**Option C: Use asset catalogs properly**

Instead of individual PNG files, fully utilize .appiconset folders with all sizes:
- 120x120 (iPhone @2x)
- 180x180 (iPhone @3x)  
- 152x152 (iPad @2x)
- 167x167 (iPad Pro @2x)

This requires updating each .appiconset/Contents.json to reference multiple sizes.

### Recommendation

**For now:** Option B (ignore warning) - app works fine on iPad

**For polish:** Option A (create iPad sizes) - better image quality

**For best practice:** Option C (proper asset catalogs) - most maintainable

### Implementation (Option A - Quick Fix)

```bash
cd LMS_StreamTest/LMS_StreamTest
for icon in Gradient HiFi Monochrome Neon Outrun Red Retro Reverse White Wordmark WordmarkWhite; do
  # Create 152x152 for iPad @2x
  sips -z 152 152 "Assets.xcassets/AppIcon-${icon}.appiconset/icon.png" \
    --out "AppIcon-${icon}@2x~ipad.png"
  
  # Create 167x167 for iPad Pro @2x
  sips -z 167 167 "Assets.xcassets/AppIcon-${icon}.appiconset/icon.png" \
    --out "AppIcon-${icon}@3x~ipad.png"
done

# Then add all 22 files to Xcode project with target membership
```

### Priority

**P3 (Low)** - Non-blocking warning, app works fine on iPad
- TestFlight works
- App Store submission works
- Just a polish/quality recommendation

Can be addressed post-launch if needed.

title: tvOS Queue: AsyncImage on long lists has no shared cache
description: QueueView fetches up to 9999 tracks. List lazy-renders, but each visible row's AsyncImage spawns its own URLSession.shared dataTask with no app-level dedupe. On Apple TV (constrained heap), scrolling through a 1000+ row queue with 200x200 JPEGs can spike memory. Practical playlists are 10-200 tracks so this rarely bites. Mitigations: (a) cap status fetch at e.g. 500, (b) implement a small URLImageCache keyed on coverID/trackID, (c) when a shared ArtworkCache singleton is built (LMS_StreamTest-... follow-up), use that. Defer until reported in practice.
close_reason: Resolved by CachedAsyncImage in commit 4644093 (same shared fix as -8uq). MediaRow — used by Queue and all other tvOS lists — now caches decoded images process-wide via NSCache, surviving List row recycling. Ships in tvOS build 5.

title: Migrate CarPlay displayUpNextQueue to shared PlaylistTrack.parseLoop
description: CarPlaySceneDelegate.swift:481 (displayUpNextQueue) parses playlist_loop dicts inline rather than via the parsePlaylistTracks helper. After 98q.6 extracts parsePlaylistTracks to PlaylistTrack.parseLoop(_:) static, CarPlay has two parse paths. Consolidation reduces drift. Note: status response embeds extra fields (playlist_cur_index, playlist_tracks) alongside playlist_loop — the migration must preserve those reads even if the loop parsing is delegated. Lower priority; CarPlay is shipping and untouched.

title: tvOS: brief double-connect race on app startup
description:
When tvOS app launches and tvOS ContentView's .onAppear fires startPlayerRegistration() -> coordinator.connect(), the SlimProtoConnectionManager's network-availability handler ALSO fires attemptReconnection() at roughly the same time. The second connect attempt is rejected cleanly by CocoaAsyncSocket:

  Connection error: Attempting to connect while connected or accepting connections. Disconnect first.

Harmless (CocoaAsyncSocket protects the existing connection), but noisy in logs and could mask real issues during diagnostics.

## Possible fixes
- Coordinator-side: idempotency guard in connect() that checks isConnecting state
- ContentView-side: remove .onAppear connect() and let only the connection manager's network-restored path fire
- Both: add a 'connect intent' debouncer

## Files
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoCoordinator.swift:152 (connect())
- LMS_StreamTest/SlimProtoConnectionManager.swift (network handler)
- LMS_StreamTest-tvOS/ContentView.swift (.onAppear)

description:
